title.zh: 卷四百八十 列傳第二百三十九 世家三 吳越錢氏錢俶(子:惟濬 惟治 惟濟 弟:儼 姪:昱 附:孫承祐 沈承禮)
title.en: Volume 480 Biographies 239: Hereditary Houses 3 - Wu, Yue, and Qian clans Qian Chu (sons: Wei Jun, Wei Zhi, Wei Ji, younger brother: Yan, nephew: Yu, relatives: Sun Chengyou, Shen Chengli)
title.raw: 卷四百八十 列傳第二百三十九 世家三 吳越錢氏錢俶(子:惟濬 惟治 惟濟 弟:儼 姪:昱 附:孫承祐 沈承禮) Volume 480 Biographies 239: Hereditary Houses 3 - Wu, Yue, and Qian clans Qian Chu (sons: Wei Jun, Wei Zhi, Wei Ji, younger brother: Yan, nephew: Yu, relatives: Sun Chengyou, Shen Chengli)

sentences.zh: 吳越錢俶字文德，杭州臨安人。

translations.literal: Qian Chu of Wuyue, courtesy name Wendé, was a native of Lin'an in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu of Wuyue, whose courtesy name was Wendé, came from Lin'an in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 本名弘俶，以犯宣祖偏諱去之。

translations.literal: His original name was Hong Chu; the character Hong was removed because it violated the partial taboo on the founding ancestor's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Hong Chu but dropped the character Hong to avoid the partial taboo on the founding emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 祖鏐，因黃巢之亂，據有吳越，昭宗授以杭、越兩藩節制，封彭城郡王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liu, amid Huang Chao's rebellion, seized Wu and Yue; Emperor Zhaozong granted him jurisdiction over the Hang and Yue circuits and enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian Liu had seized Wu and Yue during Huang Chao's rebellion; Emperor Zhaozong appointed him military commissioner over the Hang and Yue circuits and created him Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 曆梁、後唐，加吳越國王，卒，子元瓘嗣。

translations.literal: Through the Liang and Later Tang dynasties he was further created King of Wuyue; when he died, his son Yuan Guan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through the Liang and Later Tang, was further enfeoffed as King of Wuyue, and on his death his son Yuan Guan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 元瓘卒，子佐嗣。

translations.literal: When Yuan Guan died, his son Zuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guan died and was succeeded by his son Zuo.

sentences.zh: 佐卒，弟倧嗣，為其大將胡進思所廢，遂迎立俶，事具《五代史》。

translations.literal: When Zuo died, his younger brother Cong succeeded but was deposed by his great general Hu Jinsi, who then welcomed and enthroned Chu; the full account is given in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuo died his younger brother Cong took the throne, only to be deposed by his chief general Hu Jinsi, who then installed Chu; the details appear in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 俶即元瓘之第九子也，母吳越國恭懿夫人吳氏。

translations.literal: Chu was the ninth son of Yuan Guan; his mother was Lady Wu, the Respectful and Gracious Lady of the State of Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was Yuan Guan's ninth son; his mother was Lady Wu, titled the Respectful and Gracious Lady of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 晉開運中，為台州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyun era of Jin he served as prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyun period of Later Jin he was appointed prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，有僧德詔語俶曰：「此地非君為治之所，當速歸，不然不利。」

translations.literal: After several months a monk named Déshào said to Chu, "This place is not where you should govern; you should return quickly, or it will go ill for you."
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months the monk Déshào told him, "This is not a place fit for you to rule—you must return at once, or misfortune will follow."

sentences.zh: 俶從其言，即求歸國，未幾，有進思之變。

translations.literal: Chu followed his advice and at once sought to return home; before long the coup by Hu Jinsi took place.
translations.idiomatic: Chu heeded him and immediately asked to go home; not long afterward Hu Jinsi's revolt broke out.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，授東南面兵馬都元帥、鎮海鎮東軍節度使、開府儀同三司、檢校太師兼中書令、杭越等州大都督、吳越國王，賜號翊聖廣運同德保定功臣，賜以金印、玉冊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyou era of Han he was appointed Grand Marshal of the Southeast Armies, military commissioner of the Zhenhai and Zhendong circuits, Grand Preceptor with the ceremonial rank of Grand Tutor, acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Grand Governor of Hang, Yue, and other prefectures, and King of Wuyue, granted the title of Merit Subject Who Assists the Sage, Extends Fortune, Shares Virtue, and Preserves Tranquility, and presented with a gold seal and jade book.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyou reign of Later Han he received a cluster of grand appointments—Grand Marshal of the Southeast Armies, dual military commissioner over Zhenhai and Zhendong, Grand Preceptor with Grand Tutor honors, acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, Grand Governor of Hang and Yue, and King of Wuyue—along with the merit title Assisting the Sage, Extending Fortune, Sharing Virtue, and Preserving Tranquility, plus a gold seal and jade register.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南遣其將查文徽攻福州，俶發兵擒文徽，獻捷，加尚書令。

translations.literal: In the third year the Southern Tang sent its general Zha Wenhui to attack Fuzhou; Chu raised troops, captured Wenhui, and reported victory, and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Jiangnan dispatched General Zha Wenhui against Fuzhou; Chu marched out, captured Wenhui, and sent word of victory, earning promotion to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，授天下兵馬大元帥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong he was appointed Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 1 he was made Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 俶舅寧國軍節度吳延福有異圖，左右勸俶誅之，俶曰：「先夫人同氣，安忍置於法？」

translations.literal: Chu's maternal uncle Wu Yanfu, military commissioner of the Ningguo circuit, harbored disloyal designs; his attendants urged Chu to execute him, but Chu said, "He shares blood with my late mother—how could I bear to subject him to the law?"
translations.idiomatic: His uncle by marriage Wu Yanfu, Ningguo military commissioner, plotted treason; courtiers urged execution, but Chu replied, "He was my mother's own kin—how could I bring myself to punish him by law?"

sentences.zh: 言訖鳴咽流涕，但黜延福於外，終全母族。

translations.literal: Having spoken he sobbed and wept; he only banished Yanfu abroad and in the end preserved his mother's clan intact.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down in tears as he spoke, merely demoting Yanfu to an outside post and ultimately sparing his mother's entire line.

sentences.zh: 自太祖受命，俶貢奉有加常數。

translations.literal: From the time the Founding Emperor received the Mandate, Chu's tribute offerings exceeded the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu took the throne, Chu's tribute payments consistently surpassed the standing allotment.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣使賜俶戰馬二百、羊五千、橐駝三十。

translations.literal: In the second year the court sent envoys granting Chu two hundred war horses, five thousand sheep, and thirty camels.
translations.idiomatic: In year two envoys bestowed two hundred war horses, five thousand sheep, and thirty camels upon him.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，以白金萬兩、犀牙各十株、香藥一十五萬斤、金銀真珠玳瑁器數百事來貢，改賜承家保國宣德守道忠正恭順功臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande he came to court with tribute of ten thousand taels of white gold, ten pieces each of rhinoceros horn and ivory, one hundred fifty thousand jin of aromatics, and several hundred items of gold, silver, pearl, and tortoiseshell ware, and was re-granted the merit title Merit Subject Who Upholds the Family, Preserves the State, Extends Virtue, Guards the Way, Loyal, Upright, Respectful, and Obedient.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 1 he presented ten thousand taels of white gold, ten rhinoceros horns and ten ivory tusks, one hundred fifty thousand jin of incense, and hundreds of gold, silver, pearl, and tortoiseshell vessels, and in return received the new merit title Upholding the Family, Preserving the State, Extending Virtue, Guarding the Way, Loyal, Upright, Respectful, and Obedient.

sentences.zh: 是冬，郊祀，遣其子惟濬入貢。

translations.literal: That winter, when the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice, Chu sent his son Wei Jun to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, during the suburban sacrifice, he dispatched his son Wei Jun to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，改賜開吳鎮越崇文耀武宣德守道功臣，封其妻孫氏為賢德順穆夫人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was re-granted the merit title Merit Subject Who Opens Wu, Pacifies Yue, Honors Culture, Displays Martial Glory, Extends Virtue, and Guards the Way, and his wife Lady Sun was created Lady of Virtuous Deportment, Gentle Compliance, and Reverent Mildness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 5 his merit title became Opening Wu, Pacifying Yue, Honoring Culture, Displaying Martial Glory, Extending Virtue, and Guarding the Way, and his wife Lady Sun was ennobled as Lady of Virtuous Deportment, Gentle Compliance, and Reverent Mildness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遣幕吏黃夷簡入貢，上謂之曰：「汝歸語元帥，常訓練兵甲，江南強倔不朝，我將發師討之，元帥當助我，無惑人言雲『皮之不存，毛將安傅』」。

translations.literal: Before long he sent his staff officer Huang Yijian to present tribute; the emperor told him, "When you return, tell the Grand Marshal to train his arms and armor constantly. Jiangnan is strong and defiant and does not attend court—I am about to send troops to chastise them. The Grand Marshal should aid me, and not be misled by talk that 'when the skin is gone, where will the hair attach?'"
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his aide Huang Yijian came with tribute; the emperor said to him, "Go back and tell your Grand Marshal to keep drilling his forces. Jiangnan is stubborn and refuses to submit—I will march against it, and your master must help me. Do not heed those who say, 'When the skin is stripped away, on what will the hair cling?'"

sentences.zh: 特命有司造大第於薰風門外，連互數坊，棟宇宏麗，儲待什物無不悉具。

translations.literal: The authorities were specially ordered to build a great mansion outside the Xunfeng Gate, spanning several wards, with magnificent halls and storerooms fully stocked with every requisite.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially commissioned a grand residence outside the Xunfeng Gate, several wards wide, with splendid buildings and storerooms furnished down to the last detail.

sentences.zh: 因召進奉使錢文贄謂之曰：「朕數年前令學士承旨陶穀草詔，比來城南建離宮，令賜名『禮賢宅』，以待李煜及汝主，先來朝者以賜之。」

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned the tribute envoy Qian Wenzan and said to him, "Years ago I had Academician Expositor Tao Gu draft an edict. Recently a detached palace was built south of the capital, which I have named the Estate for Honoring the Worthy, to await Li Yu and your lord—whoever comes to court first shall receive it."
translations.idiomatic: He next summoned tribute envoy Qian Wenzan and said, "Some years back I ordered Academician Expositor Tao Gu to draft a proclamation. I have lately built a separate palace south of the capital and named it the Estate for Honoring the Worthy, to house Li Yu and your master—whichever arrives first will be given it."

sentences.zh: 詔以草示文贄，遂遣文贄賜俶戰馬及羊，諭旨於俶。

translations.literal: He showed Wenzan the draft edict, then sent Wenzan to bestow war horses and sheep upon Chu and convey the imperial message.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor displayed the draft to Wenzan, then sent him to grant Chu war horses and sheep and deliver the imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，賜俶襲衣、玉帶、玉鞍勒馬、金器二百兩、銀器三千兩、錦綺千段。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year Chu was granted court robes, a jade belt, a jade-trimmed saddle and bridle with horse, two hundred taels of gold vessels, three thousand taels of silver vessels, and a thousand bolts of brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year seven he received court dress, a jade belt, a horse with jade saddle and bridle, two hundred taels of goldware, three thousand taels of silverware, and a thousand lengths of brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 是冬，討江南。

translations.literal: That winter the court campaigned against Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the dynasty launched the campaign against Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 遣內客省使丁德裕齎詔，以俶為升州東面招撫製置使，賜戰馬二百匹、旌旗劍甲；

translations.literal: The Inner Palace Envoy Ding Deyu was sent bearing an edict appointing Chu Pacification and Disposition Commissioner on the eastern front of Shengzhou, and granting two hundred war horses together with banners, flags, swords, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Envoy Ding Deyu carried an edict naming Chu Pacification Commissioner on the eastern approach to Shengzhou and gifting two hundred war horses plus banners, flags, swords, and armor.

sentences.zh: 令德裕以禁兵步騎千人為俶前鋒，盡護其軍。

translations.literal: Deyu was ordered to give Chu a vanguard of one thousand infantry and cavalry from the imperial guard and to escort his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Deyu was to lead a thousand imperial guards as Chu's vanguard and protect his whole force.

sentences.zh: 李煜貽書於俶，其略曰：「今日無我，明日豈有君？

translations.literal: Li Yu sent Chu a letter, in substance: "If I am gone today, will you still be here tomorrow?
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu wrote to him, in essence: "Today there is no me—tomorrow will there be a you?

sentences.zh: 一旦明天子易地酬勳，王亦大梁一布衣耳。」

translations.literal: Once the Son of Heaven exchanges land to reward merit, you too will be but a commoner of the Great Liang."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor redistributes territory to reward service, you will be no more than a plain citizen of the great court."

sentences.zh: 俶不答，以書來上。

translations.literal: Chu did not reply but forwarded the letter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chu made no answer; he sent the letter on to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 八年，俶率兵拔常州，加守太師，詔俶歸國。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chu led troops to capture Changzhou and was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor; an edict ordered him to return to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he took Changzhou at the head of his army and was made acting Grand Preceptor; the court then ordered him home.

sentences.zh: 俶遣大將沈承禮等率兵水陸隨王師平潤州，遂進討金陵。

translations.literal: Chu dispatched his great generals Shen Chengli and others to lead land and naval forces in following the imperial army to pacify Runzhou, then advanced to besiege Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shen Chengli and other chief generals with combined land and river forces to follow the imperial host in reducing Runzhou, then pressed on against Jinling.

sentences.zh: 上嘗召進奏使任知果，令諭旨於俶曰：「元帥克毗陵有大功，俟平江南，可暫來與朕相見，以慰延想之意。

translations.literal: The emperor once summoned Memorial Presenter Ren Zhiguo and had him convey to Chu, "The Grand Marshal's capture of Piling was a great achievement. When Jiangnan is pacified you may come briefly to see me and ease my longing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called in Memorial Presenter Ren Zhiguo and told him to say to Chu, "Your seizure of Piling was a major feat. Once Jiangnan falls, come for a short visit to satisfy my yearning to meet you.

sentences.zh: 即當遣還，不久留也。

translations.literal: You will then be sent back—I will not detain you long.
translations.idiomatic: I will send you home at once and will not keep you long.

sentences.zh: 朕三執圭幣以見上帝，豈食言乎？」

translations.literal: Three times I have held the jade scepter and libation cups before Heaven—would I break my word?"
translations.idiomatic: Three times I have offered the jade tablet and libation vessels before Heaven—do you think I would lie?"

sentences.zh: 江南平，論功以俶大將沈承禮、孫承祐並為節度使，為防禦使者一人、刺史六人。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, for merit Chu's great generals Shen Chengli and Sun Chengyou were both made military commissioners, with one made defense commissioner and six made prefects.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan fell, Shen Chengli and Sun Chengyou, Chu's chief generals, were each appointed military commissioner, one defense commissioner, and six prefects.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，俶與其妻孫氏、子惟濬、平江軍節度使孫承祐來朝，上遣皇子興元尹德昭至睢陽迎勞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year Chu came to court with his wife Lady Sun, his son Wei Jun, and Sun Chengyou, military commissioner of the Pingjiang army; the emperor sent his son, Prince of Xingyuan De Zhao, to Suiyang to welcome and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year nine Chu arrived at court with Lady Sun, Wei Jun, and Pingjiang military commissioner Sun Chengyou; the emperor sent Prince De Zhao of Xingyuan to Suiyang to receive him.

sentences.zh: 俶將至，車駕先幸禮賢宅，按視供帳之具。

translations.literal: Before Chu arrived the imperial carriage went first to the Estate for Honoring the Worthy to inspect the furnishings prepared for his lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came the emperor himself visited the Estate for Honoring the Worthy to review the quarters prepared for him.

sentences.zh: 及至，詔俶居之。

translations.literal: When he arrived an edict directed that Chu lodge there.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival an edict assigned him residence there.

sentences.zh: 對於崇德殿，貢白金四萬兩、絹五萬匹，賜襲衣、玉帶、金器千兩、白金器三千兩、羅綺三千段、玉勒馬。

translations.literal: He was received in audience at the Chongde Hall and presented forty thousand taels of white gold and fifty thousand bolts of silk; he was granted court robes, a jade belt, one thousand taels of gold vessels, three thousand taels of platinum vessels, three thousand lengths of silk gauze, and a horse with jade bridle.
translations.idiomatic: At audience in the Chongde Hall he offered forty thousand taels of white gold and fifty thousand bolts of silk and received court dress, a jade belt, a thousand taels of goldware, three thousand taels of platinumware, three thousand bolts of gauze and silk, and a jade-bridled horse.

sentences.zh: 即日宴長春殿，俶又貢白金二萬兩、絹三萬匹、乳香二萬斤。

translations.literal: That same day a banquet was held in the Changchun Hall; Chu again presented twenty thousand taels of white gold, thirty thousand bolts of silk, and twenty thousand jin of frankincense.
translations.idiomatic: The same day he was feasted in the Changchun Hall and again gave twenty thousand taels of white gold, thirty thousand bolts of silk, and twenty thousand jin of frankincense.

sentences.zh: 賀平江左，貢白金五萬兩、錢十萬貫、綿百八十萬兩、茶八萬五千斤、犀角象牙二百株、香藥三百斤。

translations.literal: Congratulating the pacification of the lower Yangzi, he presented fifty thousand taels of white gold, one hundred thousand strings of cash, one million eight hundred thousand taels of cotton, eighty-five thousand jin of tea, two hundred rhinoceros horns and ivory tusks, and three hundred jin of aromatics.
translations.idiomatic: To celebrate the conquest of the Jiangzuo region he sent fifty thousand taels of white gold, one hundred thousand strings of coin, one million eight hundred thousand taels of cotton, eighty-five thousand jin of tea, two hundred horns and tusks, and three hundred jin of incense.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸其第，又貢白金十萬兩、絹五萬匹、乳香五萬斤，以助郊祭。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited his residence he again presented one hundred thousand taels of white gold, fifty thousand bolts of silk, and fifty thousand jin of frankincense to assist the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor called at his lodging he added one hundred thousand taels of white gold, fifty thousand bolts of silk, and fifty thousand jin of frankincense toward the suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 三月庚午，詔曰：「古者宗工大臣特被隆眷，或劍履上殿，或書詔不名，率由豐功，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu in the third month an edict said, "In antiquity founding ministers specially received lofty favor—some were permitted swords and shoes in the palace, others had their names omitted from written edicts—all by reason of abundant merit and treated with exceptional ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's gengwu day an edict declared, "Anciently, chief ministers of founding merit enjoyed extraordinary grace—some wore sword and shoes in the throne hall, others were not named in edicts—all in reward for towering service and marked by singular ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今我兼其命數，用獎勳賢，輝映古今，允為優異。

translations.literal: Now I combine these privileges to reward meritorious worthies, a brilliance spanning past and present, truly outstanding favor.
translations.idiomatic: Today I unite these honors to reward the worthy, a splendor spanning ages and singular in its excellence.

sentences.zh: 谘爾吳越國王錢俶，德隆宏茂，器識深遠，撫奧區於吳會，勒洪伐於宗彝。

translations.literal: To you, King Qian Chu of Wuyue—your virtue is lofty and abundant, your capacity far-reaching; you have governed the Wu-Yue region and inscribed great campaigns upon the imperial temple vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Thus to you, King Qian Chu of Wuyue: your virtue is grand and your vision deep; you have ruled the Wu-Yue lands and recorded great expeditions on the ancestral bronzes.

sentences.zh: 昨以江表不庭，王師致討，委方面之兵柄，克常、潤之土宇，輔翼帝室，震疊皇靈。

translations.literal: Recently, because the south of the Yangzi would not submit, the imperial army marched to chastise; you were entrusted with command of the frontier forces and took the territories of Chang and Run, aiding the imperial house and shaking the august spirits.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower Yangzi rebelled and the court sent armies, you held regional command, seized Chang and Run, supported the throne, and awed the realm.

sentences.zh: 而乃執圭來庭，垂紳就列，罄事君之誠愨，為群後之表儀。

translations.literal: Yet you came to court holding your jade tablet, took your place with sash hanging down, and poured out the utmost loyalty of a subject, becoming a model for all the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: You then came to court with jade tablet in hand, stood in ranks with your sash, and displayed perfect loyalty, setting an example for every vassal prince.

sentences.zh: 爰峻徽章，以旌元老。

translations.literal: Therefore I elevate your title to honor an elder statesman.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I raise your honors to salute a founding elder.

sentences.zh: 可特賜劍履上殿，書詔不名。」

translations.literal: You are specially granted sword and shoes in the palace and omission of your name from written edicts."
translations.idiomatic: He is specially granted the privileges of wearing sword and shoes in the palace and of being unnamed in edicts."

sentences.zh: 以俶妻賢德順穆夫人孫氏為吳越國王妃，令惟濬齎詔賜之。

translations.literal: Chu's wife, Lady Sun of Virtuous Deportment, Gentle Compliance, and Reverent Mildness, was created Princess Consort of the State of Wuyue, and Wei Jun was ordered to carry the edict and bestow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's wife Lady Sun was created Princess Consort of Wuyue, and Wei Jun was sent to deliver the edict.

sentences.zh: 宰相以為異姓諸侯王妻無封妃之典，太祖曰：「行自我朝，表異恩也。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers held that there was no precedent for enfeoffing a princess consort upon the wife of a feudatory king of another surname; the Founding Emperor said, "Let the precedent begin in our dynasty—it marks special favor."
translations.idiomatic: The councilors objected that non-imperial clans had no precedent for creating their wives princesses; Taizu replied, "Let our court set the precedent—it signals exceptional grace."

sentences.zh: 俶獻白金六萬兩、絹六萬匹為謝。

translations.literal: Chu presented sixty thousand taels of white gold and sixty thousand bolts of silk in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chu offered sixty thousand taels of white gold and sixty thousand bolts of silk in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 太祖數詔俶與其子惟濬宴射苑中，惟諸王預坐。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor repeatedly summoned Chu and his son Wei Jun to banquets and archery in the imperial park, with the imperial princes also seated.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu often invited Chu and Wei Jun to feast and shoot in the park, the imperial princes joining them.

sentences.zh: 每宣諭俶，俶拜謝，多令內侍掖起，俶感泣。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor addressed Chu, Chu would bow in thanks; the emperor often had palace attendants raise him up, and Chu would weep with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the emperor spoke to him Chu kowtowed in gratitude; attendants were told to lift him up, and he wept moved.

sentences.zh: 又嘗一日召宴，獨太宗、秦王侍坐，酒酣，太祖令俶與太宗、秦王敘昆仲之禮，俶伏地叩頭，涕泣固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: On another day he was summoned to a banquet with only the Taizong Emperor and the Prince of Qin seated; when the wine was warm the Founding Emperor ordered Chu to exchange fraternal courtesies with them; Chu prostrated himself, weeping and firmly declining, and the order was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at a feast with only Taizong and the Prince of Qin present, Taizu bade Chu exchange brotherly courtesies with them; Chu kowtowed, weeping and refusing until the command was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 會將以四月幸西京，親雩祀，俶懇請扈從，不許，留惟濬侍祠，令俶歸國。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to go west to the secondary capital in the fourth month for the ploughing sacrifice, Chu earnestly asked to accompany him but was refused; Wei Jun was kept to attend the rites while Chu was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to visit the western capital in the fourth month for the ploughing rite, Chu begged to attend but was denied; Wei Jun remained for the ceremony while Chu returned home.

sentences.zh: 太祖宴餞於講武殿，賜窄衣、玉束帶、玉鞍勒馬、玳瑁鞭、金銀錦彩二十餘萬、銀裝兵八百事，謂俶曰：「南北風土異宜，漸及炎暑，卿可早發。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor gave a farewell banquet in the Jiangwu Hall, granting narrow-sleeved robes, a jade belt, a jade saddle and bridle with horse, a tortoiseshell whip, and more than two hundred thousand in gold, silver, and brocade, plus eight hundred silver-mounted weapons, telling Chu, "North and south differ in climate; summer heat is coming—you should depart early."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu feasted him farewell in the Jiangwu Hall with narrow robes, jade belt, jade-bridled horse, tortoiseshell whip, over two hundred thousand in gold, silver, and brocade, and eight hundred silver-mounted arms, saying, "North and south differ in climate—summer is near; leave soon."

sentences.zh: 俶涕泣言願三歲一朝，太祖曰：「川陸迂遠，當俟詔旨，即來覲也。」

translations.literal: Chu wept and said he wished to attend court once every three years; the Founding Emperor said, "The route by land and water is long—wait for an edict, then come to audience."
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, Chu asked to visit every three years; Taizu answered, "Land and water make the journey arduous—come when an edict summons you."

sentences.zh: 俶將發京師，特賜導從儀衛之物，率皆鮮麗，令自禮賢宅陳列至迎春苑。

translations.literal: As Chu was about to leave the capital he was specially granted an escort with guards and regalia, all freshly splendid, to be displayed in procession from the Estate for Honoring the Worthy to the Yingchun Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left the capital he received a special escort of guards and regalia, all new and resplendent, paraded from the Estate for Honoring the Worthy to the Yingchun Garden.

sentences.zh: 自俶之至，逮於歸國，太祖所賜金器萬兩、白金器又數萬兩、白金十餘萬兩、錦綺綾羅絹四十餘萬匹、馬數百匹，他物不可勝計。

translations.literal: From Chu's arrival until his return home the Founding Emperor's gifts included ten thousand taels of gold vessels, several tens of thousands of taels of platinum vessels, more than one hundred thousand taels of white gold, more than four hundred thousand bolts of brocade, silk, damask, and gauze, and several hundred horses—other items beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Between his arrival and departure Taizu had given him ten thousand taels of goldware, tens of thousands of taels of platinumware, over one hundred thousand taels of white gold, more than four hundred thousand bolts of silks, and hundreds of horses, besides innumerable other gifts.

sentences.zh: 俶既歸國，嘗視事功臣堂，一日命坐於東偏，謂左右曰：「西北者神京在焉，天威不違顏咫尺，俶豈敢寧居乎？」

translations.literal: After Chu returned home he once held court in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers and ordered a seat placed on the east side, telling his attendants, "To the northwest lies the divine capital—the imperial majesty is but a stone's throw away; how could I sit at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: Back in his realm he once held audience in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers and had a seat set on the east, saying to his staff, "The sacred capital lies to the northwest—Heaven's majesty is within a stone's throw; how dare I sit comfortably?"

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，加食邑五千戶。

translations.literal: When the Taizong Emperor succeeded to the throne Chu's fief income was increased by five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession five thousand households were added to his fief income.

sentences.zh: 俶貢禦衣，通天犀帶，絹萬匹，金器、玳瑁器百餘事，金銀扣器五百事，塗金銀香台、龍腦檀香床、銀假果、水晶花凡數千計，價直钜萬；

translations.literal: Chu presented imperial robes, a belt of heaven-piercing rhinoceros horn, ten thousand bolts of silk, more than a hundred items of gold and tortoiseshell ware, five hundred gold- and silver-mounted vessels, and several thousand items including gilt-silver incense stands, agarwood and sandalwood beds, silver imitation fruit, and crystal flowers, worth tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: He sent imperial robes, a heaven-piercing rhinoceros-horn belt, ten thousand bolts of silk, over a hundred gold and tortoiseshell pieces, five hundred gold- and silver-mounted vessels, and thousands of objects—gilt incense stands, sandalwood beds, silver fruit, crystal flowers—worth a fortune;

sentences.zh: 又貢犀角象牙三十株、香藥萬斤、幹薑五萬斤、茶五萬斤。

translations.literal: he also presented thirty rhinoceros horns and ivory tusks, ten thousand jin of aromatics, fifty thousand jin of dried ginger, and fifty thousand jin of tea.
translations.idiomatic: plus thirty horns and tusks, ten thousand jin of incense, fifty thousand jin of dried ginger, and fifty thousand jin of tea.

sentences.zh: 俶又請歲增常貢，詔不許。

translations.literal: Chu also requested to increase his annual regular tribute; an edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to raise his yearly tribute quota; the court declined.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年正月，孫氏卒，遣給事中程羽吊祭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo Lady Sun died; the court sent Supervising Secretary Cheng Yu to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taiping Xingguo 2 Lady Sun died; Supervising Secretary Cheng Yu was dispatched to mourn.

sentences.zh: 九月，上言乞所賜詔書呼名，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he memorialized asking that edicts address him by name; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he petitioned that edicts call him by name; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，來朝，遣判四方館事梁迥至泗州迎勞；

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year he came to court; Liang Hui, Commissioner for All Four Bureaus, was sent to Sizhou to welcome and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year three he came to court; Commissioner Liang Hui was sent to Sizhou to receive him.

sentences.zh: 惟濬先在闕下，上遣至睢陽候俶。

translations.literal: Wei Jun was already at the capital; the emperor sent him to Suiyang to await Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun was already at court; the emperor sent him to Suiyang to wait for his father.

sentences.zh: 俶先遣孫承祐入奏事，上即遣承祐護諸司供帳勞俶於郊，又命齊王廷美宴俶於迎春苑。

translations.literal: Chu first sent Sun Chengyou to report; the emperor at once sent Chengyou to oversee all bureaus' preparations to honor Chu in the suburbs, and ordered Prince of Qi Tingmei to feast Chu in the Yingchun Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Chu first sent Sun Chengyou ahead; the emperor immediately had Chengyou supervise suburban preparations and ordered Prince Tingmei of Qi to entertain Chu in the Yingchun Garden.

sentences.zh: 俶至，對於崇德殿，賜襲衣、玉帶、金銀器、玉鞍勒馬、錦彩萬匹、錢千萬；

translations.literal: When Chu arrived he was received at the Chongde Hall and granted court robes, a jade belt, gold and silver vessels, a jade saddle and bridle with horse, ten thousand bolts of brocade and silk, and ten million cash.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was received in the Chongde Hall and given court dress, jade belt, gold and silver vessels, jade-bridled horse, ten thousand bolts of silks, and ten million cash.

sentences.zh: 賓佐崔仁冀等賜金銀帶、器幣、鞍馬有差。

translations.literal: His aides Cui Renji and others received gold and silver belts, vessels, coins, and horses in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: His staff, including Cui Renji, received gold and silver belts, goods, cash, and horses in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 即日宴俶長春殿，令劉鋹、李煜預坐。

translations.literal: That same day a banquet was held for Chu in the Changchun Hall, with Liu Chang and Li Yu also seated.
translations.idiomatic: The same day he was banqueted in the Changchun Hall, Liu Chang and Li Yu sharing the table.

sentences.zh: 俶貢白金五萬兩、錢萬萬，絹十萬匹、綾二萬匹、綿十萬，屯茶十萬斤、建茶萬斤、幹薑萬斤，越器五萬事，錦緣席千，金銀畫舫三、銀飾龍舟四，金飾烏樠木禦食案、御床各一，金樽罍盞斝各一、金飾玳瑁器三十事、金扣藤盤二、金扣雕象俎十，銀假果樹十事、翠毛真珠花三叢，七寶飾食案十、銀樽罍十、盞斝副焉，金扣越器百五十事、雕銀俎五十，密假果、剪羅花各二十樹，銀扣大盤十，銀裝鼓二、七寶飾胡琴五弦箏各四、銀飾箜篌方響羯鼓各四、紅牙樂器二十二事，乳香萬斤、犀角象牙各一百株，香藥萬斤、蘇木萬斤。

translations.literal: Chu presented fifty thousand taels of white gold, ten thousand strings of ten thousand cash, one hundred thousand bolts of silk and two thousand of damask, one hundred thousand of cotton, one hundred thousand jin of Tuntun tea and ten thousand of Jian tea, ten thousand jin of dried ginger, fifty thousand items of Yue ware, a thousand brocade-fringed mats, three gold-inlaid painted pleasure boats and four silver-trimmed dragon boats, one gold-mounted wumu imperial food table and one imperial bed, one each of gold goblets, cups, and wine vessels, thirty gold-mounted tortoiseshell items, two gold-mounted rattan trays and ten gold-mounted carved ivory stands, ten silver imitation fruit trees and three clusters of kingfisher-feather and pearl flowers, ten jewel-mounted food tables and ten silver goblets with matching cups and vessels, one hundred fifty gold-mounted Yue items and fifty carved silver stands, twenty each of honeyed imitation fruit and cut-silk flowers, ten large silver-mounted trays, two silver-mounted drums, four each of jewel-mounted five-string zithers and zithers, four each of silver-mounted konghou, square chimes, and waist drums, twenty-two red-ivory musical instruments, ten thousand jin of frankincense, one hundred each of rhinoceros horn and ivory, ten thousand jin of aromatics, and ten thousand jin of sappanwood.
translations.idiomatic: His tribute ran to fifty thousand taels of white gold, a hundred million strings of cash, vast quantities of silk, damask, cotton, teas, ginger, Yue ceramics, brocade mats, gold and silver boats and furnishings, jeweled tables, musical instruments by the score, frankincense, horns, tusks, incense, and sappanwood—an inventory almost beyond listing.

sentences.zh: 上又嘗召俶及其子惟濬宴後苑，泛舟池中，上手酌酒以賜俶，俶跪飲之。

translations.literal: The emperor also once summoned Chu and Wei Jun to feast in the rear garden and row on the pond; the emperor himself poured wine and gave it to Chu, and Chu knelt to drink.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once feasted father and son in the rear garden and rowed on the pool; he poured wine with his own hand for Chu, who knelt to drink it.

sentences.zh: 其恩待如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: His treatment was of this order.

sentences.zh: 四月，會陳洪進納土，俶上言曰：「臣伏有懇誠，貯於肺腑，幸因入覲，輒敢上聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, when Chen Hongjin surrendered his territory, Chu memorialized, "Your subject harbors a sincere plea stored in his inmost heart; fortunate to attend court in person, I venture to lay it before you.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, as Chen Hongjin surrendered his domain, Chu wrote, "I keep a heartfelt petition in my breast; having come to court, I dare present it.

sentences.zh: 蓋虞神道之害盈，必冀天慈之從欲。

translations.literal: For the Way of the Spirits abhors excess, and one must hope for Heaven's mercy to grant one's desire.
translations.idiomatic: The divine way punishes fullness—I pray only that Heaven's kindness will grant what I seek.

sentences.zh: 臣近蒙朝廷賜以劍履上殿，詔書不名，仍以本道領募卒徒，嘗營戈甲，特建國王之號，俾增師律之嚴，皆所以假其寵名，托於鄰敵。

translations.literal: Your subject has lately received from the court the privilege of sword and shoes in the palace and omission of his name from edicts, yet still leads locally recruited troops of this circuit and has maintained arms and armor, and was specially granted the title of King of Wuyue—all merely to borrow a grand name as a shield against neighboring foes.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately been granted sword and shoes in the palace and anonymity in edicts, yet still command locally raised troops and keep armor, and was given the title King of Wuyue—all merely borrowed grandeur to face neighboring enemies.

sentences.zh: 方今幅員開外，名數洞分，豈可冒居，自罹公議？

translations.literal: Now the realm is open on every side and titles are clearly distinguished—how could I presumptuously hold such rank and bring public censure upon myself?
translations.idiomatic: Now the empire is unified and ranks are clearly ordered—how could I cling to such titles and invite reproach?

sentences.zh: 合從省罷，以正等威。

translations.literal: They ought to be abolished to set authority right.
translations.idiomatic: They should be removed to restore proper dignity.

sentences.zh: 除本道軍士、器甲臣已曾奏納外，其所封吳越國王及天下兵馬大元帥職名，望皆許解罷。

translations.literal: Apart from the troops and armor of this circuit, which your subject has already memorialized surrendering, I beg that the titles King of Wuyue and Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven may all be relinquished.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the circuit's soldiers and arms I have already offered, I ask that the titles King of Wuyue and Grand Marshal of All Armies be abolished.

sentences.zh: 凡頒詔命，願復名呼，庶聖朝無虛授之恩，微臣免疾顛之禍。」

translations.literal: As for all edicts hereafter, I wish my name to be spoken again, so that the sacred court suffers no empty grant of favor and your humble subject escapes the calamity of presumptuous excess."
translations.idiomatic: For future edicts I ask that my name be used again, lest the court grant honors in vain and I suffer ruin from overreaching."

sentences.zh: 優詔不許。

translations.literal: A gracious edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of favor declined the request.

sentences.zh: 五月乙酉，俶再上表：「臣慶遇承平之運，遠修肆覲之儀，宸眷彌隆，寵章皆極。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou in the fifth month Chu again submitted a memorial: "Your subject rejoices to live in an age of peace and has come from afar to perform the audience rite; imperial favor grows ever richer and every bestowal reaches the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth month's yiyou day he submitted again: "I rejoice in this peaceful age and have come from afar to perform court ritual; your grace deepens and every gift is supreme.

sentences.zh: 鬥筲之量實覺滿盈，丹赤之誠輒茲披露。

translations.literal: The measure of a peck and dipper feels truly full; with utmost crimson sincerity I now disclose it.
translations.idiomatic: My small measure is truly overflowing; with utmost sincerity I now reveal it.

sentences.zh: 臣伏念祖宗以來，親提義旅，尊戴中京，略有兩浙之土田，討平一方之僭逆。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that since our ancestors first raised the banner of righteousness and honored the central court, we have held somewhat more than the two Zhe circuits' lands and suppressed rebellion in one region.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that our forebears first raised righteous arms, honored the central capital, held the two Zhe circuits, and quelled local usurpers.

sentences.zh: 此際蓋隔朝天之路，莫諧請吏之心。

translations.literal: At that time the road to the imperial court was cut off and the heart to register as subjects could not be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Then the path to court was blocked and we could not fulfill our wish to submit registers.

sentences.zh: 然而稟號令於闕庭，保封疆於邊徼，家世承襲，已及百年。

translations.literal: Yet we received orders from the palace and preserved our border marches; the line has passed down in succession for nearly a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Still we took orders from the throne and guarded our frontier; the house has ruled in succession for nearly a century.

sentences.zh: 今者幸遇皇帝陛下嗣守丕基，削平諸夏，凡在率濱之內，悉歸輿地之圖。

translations.literal: Now, fortunately encountering Your Majesty succeeding to the great foundation and pacifying all Xia, all within the four seas who bear allegiance return to the imperial map.
translations.idiomatic: Now, under Your Majesty who has inherited the great enterprise and pacified all realms, every shore submits to the imperial domain.

sentences.zh: 獨臣一邦僻介江表，職貢雖陳於外府，版籍未歸於有司，尚令山越之民，猶隔陶唐之化。

translations.literal: Only my single state lies remote on the south of the Yangzi; though tribute has been offered to the outer court, our registers have not been returned to the authorities, and the people of the hills and marshes remain apart from the civilization of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Only my small realm remains apart on the Jiangnan coast; though tribute reaches the outer court, our registers are not with the ministries, and hill folk still stand outside imperial transformation.

sentences.zh: 太陽委照，不及蔀家，春雷發聲，兀為聾俗，則臣實使之然也，罪莫大焉。

translations.literal: The sun shines but does not reach a thatched roof; spring thunder sounds but the deaf hear nothing—this is truly because of your subject, and the crime could not be greater.
translations.idiomatic: The sun shines yet a humble roof is shaded; thunder rolls yet the deaf hear nothing—it is my fault alone, and no crime could be greater.

sentences.zh: 不勝大願，願以所管十三州獻於闕下執事，其間地裏名數別具條析以聞。

translations.literal: Unable to bear it, I wish to present the thirteen prefectures under my rule to the court; their lands, boundaries, and designations will be set forth in a separate detailed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear it and beg to surrender the thirteen prefectures I govern to the throne, with their boundaries and names listed in a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下念奕世之忠勤，察乃心之傾向，特降明詔，允茲至誠。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will consider the loyalty of many generations and discern the inclination of my heart, and will specially issue a bright edict granting this utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will weigh generations of loyalty, see the bent of my heart, and issue a clear edict accepting this utmost devotion."

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「卿世濟忠純，誌遵憲度，承百年之堂構，有千里之江山。

translations.literal: The reply edict said, "You have for generations maintained pure loyalty, your will observant of law; you inherit a century's patrimony and a thousand-li realm.
translations.idiomatic: The response read, "Your house has for generations kept pure loyalty and observed the statutes; you inherit a century's estate and a thousand-li domain.

sentences.zh: 自朕纂臨，聿修覲禮，睹文物之全盛，喜書軌之混同，願親日月之光，遽忘江海之志。

translations.literal: Since I ascended the throne I have restored the audience rites; beholding the full splendor of culture, I rejoice that writing and cart tracks are unified; you wished to draw near the sun and moon's light and suddenly forgot the resolve of rivers and seas.
translations.idiomatic: Since my accession I have restored court ritual; seeing culture in full flower, I rejoice that script and roads are one; you sought the sun and moon's radiance and at once set aside the ambition of rivers and seas.

sentences.zh: 甲兵樓櫓既悉上於有司，山川土田又盡獻於天府，舉宗效順，前代所無，書之簡編，永彰忠烈。

translations.literal: Arms, towers, and ships have all been surrendered to the authorities; mountains, rivers, and fields are now fully presented to the imperial treasury—such complete submission by an entire clan has no precedent in earlier ages; recorded in the annals it will forever display loyal valor.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons, towers, and fleets are with the ministries; land and rivers enter the imperial store—never before has a whole clan submitted so completely; let the annals record this loyalty forever.

sentences.zh: 所請宜依。」

translations.literal: Your request is approved."
translations.idiomatic: It is granted as requested."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「漢寵功臣，聿著帶河之誓；

translations.literal: On the day dinghai an edict said, "In Han, meritorious ministers were favored and the oath by the Yellow River was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict declared, "The Han honored their ministers with the pledge sworn by the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 周尊元老，遂分表海之邦。

translations.literal: In Zhou the elders were revered and coastal states beyond the sea were apportioned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou the senior statesmen were honored and realms beyond the sea were divided among them.

sentences.zh: 其有奄宅勾吳，早綿星紀，包茅入貢，不絕於累朝，羽檄起兵，備嘗於百戰。

translations.literal: There are those who long held Gouwu territory, early bound to the stars of Wu, who sent wrapped grass as tribute through successive dynasties without cease and raised armies on urgent dispatches, having tasted a hundred battles.
translations.idiomatic: Some have long ruled Gouwu lands, tied to Wu's constellations since antiquity, presenting tribute through age after age and marching to war at every urgent call, veterans of a hundred campaigns.

sentences.zh: 適當輯瑞而來勤，爰以提封而上獻。

translations.literal: Now, meeting the season of gathering auspicious jade, they have come in diligence and offered their domains aloft.
translations.idiomatic: Now, coming at this season of tribute and loyalty, they have presented their territories to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宜遷內地，別錫爰田，彌昭啟土之榮，俾增書社之數。

translations.literal: They should be moved to the interior and granted separate fields, further displaying the glory of enfeoffment and increasing their allotment of sacrificial lands.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be resettled inland with new estates, magnifying the honor of founding a state and adding to their sacrificial fiefs.

sentences.zh: 吳越國王錢俶天資純懿，世濟忠貞，兆積德於靈源，書大勳於策府。

translations.literal: King Qian Chu of Wuyue is pure and excellent by nature, loyal through the generations, with accumulated virtue at the source of his line and great merit recorded in the imperial archives.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu of Wuyue is innately upright, his house loyal for generations, virtue gathered at its fountainhead and great deeds inscribed in the dynastic records.

sentences.zh: 近者慶衝人之踐阼，奉國珍而來朝，齒革羽毛既修其常貢，土田版籍又獻於有司，願宿衛於京師，表乃心於王室。

translations.literal: Recently, rejoicing at the young ruler's accession, he brought the state's treasures to court; hides, leather, and feathers fulfilled his regular tribute, and land registers were surrendered to the authorities; he wished to guard the capital as a sign of loyalty to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, celebrating the emperor's accession, he came with state treasures; routine tribute of hides and plumes was complete, and land registers were delivered to the ministries; he asked to serve at court as proof of devotion to the throne.

sentences.zh: 眷茲誠節，宜茂寵光。

translations.literal: Considering such sincerity, his honors should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: In view of this loyalty, his rewards should be magnified.

sentences.zh: 是用列西楚之名區，析長淮之奧壤，建茲大國，不遠舊封，載疏千里之疆，更重四征之寄。

translations.literal: Therefore the great name-region of Western Chu and the rich lands along the long Huai are delineated to establish this great state, not far from his former enfeoffment, spanning a thousand li and again entrusting him with the charge of the four expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: The celebrated region of Western Chu and the fertile Huai heartland are set apart to found this great kingdom, near his old domain, a thousand-li territory with renewed trust as commander of the four campaigns.

sentences.zh: 疇其爵邑，施及子孫，永夾輔於皇家，用對揚於休命，垂厥百世，不其偉歟！

translations.literal: His fiefs and estates extend to his sons and grandsons; may they forever flank the imperial house and answer this glorious mandate—lasting a hundred generations: how grand!
translations.idiomatic: His titles and lands pass to his descendants; may they forever support the throne and answer this splendid charge—a legacy for a hundred generations, how magnificent!

sentences.zh: 其以淮南節度管內封俶為淮海國王，仍改賜寧淮鎮海崇文耀武宣德守道功臣，即以禮賢宅賜之。」

translations.literal: Within the Huainan circuit let Chu be enfeoffed as King of the Huaihai Kingdom, re-granted the merit title Pacifying the Huai, Pacifying the Sea, Honoring Culture, Displaying Martial Glory, Extending Virtue, and Guarding the Way, and the Estate for Honoring the Worthy is bestowed upon him."
translations.idiomatic: He is created King of Huaihai over the Huainan circuit, given the merit title Pacifying Huai and Sea, Honoring Culture, Displaying Martial Glory, Extending Virtue, and Guarding the Way, and granted the Estate for Honoring the Worthy."

sentences.zh: 惟濬為節度使兼侍中，惟治為節度使，惟演為團練使，惟願暨侄鬱、昱並為刺史，弟儀、信並為觀察使，將校孫承祐、沈承禮並為節度使。

translations.literal: Wei Jun was made military commissioner and concurrent Palace Attendant; Wei Zhi military commissioner; Wei Yan regimental commander; Wei Yuan together with nephews Yu and Yu were all made prefects; younger brothers Yi and Xin observation commissioners; generals Sun Chengyou and Shen Chengli both military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun became military commissioner and Palace Attendant; Wei Zhi military commissioner; Wei Yan regimental commander; Wei Yuan with nephews Yu and Yu were made prefects; brothers Yi and Xin observation commissioners; Sun Chengyou and Shen Chengli were made military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 體貌隆盛，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: His stature and honors were lofty, unmatched in his age.
translations.idiomatic: His honors and presence towered above all his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 是歲七月中元，京城張燈，令有司於俶宅前設燈山、陳聲樂以寵之。

translations.literal: That year at the mid-year festival in the seventh month lanterns were hung in the capital; the authorities were ordered to set a lantern mountain and stage music before Chu's residence to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month, during the mid-year lantern festival, officials erected a lantern mountain and music before his house in special favor.

sentences.zh: 八月，令兩浙發俶緦麻以上親及管內官吏悉歸朝，凡舟一千四十四艘，所過以兵護送。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the two Zhe circuits were ordered to send all of Chu's kin in mourning dress and above and all officials within his jurisdiction to court—one thousand forty-four boats in all, escorted by troops wherever they passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month both Zhe circuits sent every relative in mourning dress and every local official to court—one thousand forty-four vessels, troops escorting each along the route.

sentences.zh: 杭州貢俶樂人凡八十有一人，詔以三十六人還杭州，四十五人賜俶。

translations.literal: Hangzhou presented eighty-one musicians for Chu; an edict returned thirty-six to Hangzhou and granted forty-five to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou sent eighty-one musicians; the court sent thirty-six back and gave forty-five to Chu.

sentences.zh: 俶上表謝，上親畫「付中書送史館」。

translations.literal: Chu memorialized thanks; the emperor personally wrote "Deliver to the Secretariat and send to the Historiographical Office."
translations.idiomatic: Chu thanked him in a memorial; the emperor personally wrote, "Send this to the Secretariat for the Historical Office."

sentences.zh: 四年二月宴苑中，俶被病拜不能起，上命以銀裝肩輿送歸，因以賜之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, at a garden banquet Chu fell ill and could not rise to bow; the emperor ordered him carried back in a silver-mounted sedan chair and then gave him the chair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, second month, at a garden feast Chu was too ill to bow; the emperor had him borne home in a silver sedan and then gave him the chair.

sentences.zh: 四月，從征太原，賜羊三百、酒十斛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he accompanied the campaign against Taiyuan and was granted three hundred sheep and ten hu of wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he followed the Taiyuan expedition and received three hundred sheep and ten hu of wine.

sentences.zh: 俶小心謹恪，每晨趨行闕，人未有至者，必先至，假寐以待旦。

translations.literal: Chu was cautious and respectful; each morning he hurried to the palace gate—before anyone else arrived he was already there, dozing until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly careful, each dawn he reached the palace before anyone else and waited, half asleep, for daybreak.

sentences.zh: 上知之，謂俶曰：「卿已中年，宜避風冷，自今入謁不須太早也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor learned of it he told Chu, "You are already middle-aged; you should avoid wind and cold—from now on you need not come so early to audience."
translations.idiomatic: Learning this, the emperor said, "You are no longer young—avoid the cold winds; hereafter do not come to audience so early."

sentences.zh: 特輟御前二大燭以賜之，令先赴前頓。

translations.literal: He specially set aside two great candles from before the throne to give him and ordered him to go first to the forward camp.
translations.idiomatic: He specially granted two imperial candles and told him to go ahead to the advance camp.

sentences.zh: 上嘗賜從臣食於中路頓，並賜衛士羊臂臑、卮酒，觀其飲啖。

translations.literal: The emperor once feasted his followers at a midway halt and also gave the guards lamb shoulder and cups of wine, watching how they ate and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a roadside halt he feasted his attendants and gave the guards lamb shoulder and wine, observing how they ate.

sentences.zh: 上見其雄壯，因顧俶，俶進曰：「所謂『如虎如貔、如熊如羆』者也。」

translations.literal: Seeing how stalwart they were, he turned to Chu; Chu advanced and said, "These are what is meant by 'like tigers and leopards, like bears and brown bears.'"
translations.idiomatic: Struck by their vigor, he looked at Chu, who said, "These are the men of whom the ode says, 'like tigers and leopards, like bears and grizzlies.'"

sentences.zh: 會劉繼元降，上御連城台誅軍中先亡命太原者，顧謂俶曰：「卿能保全一方以歸於我，不致血刃，深可嘉也。」

translations.literal: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered the emperor ascended the Linked Walls terrace to execute deserters from the army who had fled to Taiyuan, and said to Chu, "You were able to preserve a whole region and return it to me without bloodshed—deeply admirable."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered the emperor executed deserters at the Linked Walls terrace and told Chu, "You brought an entire region back to me without bloodshed—this is greatly to be praised."

sentences.zh: 俶頓首謝。

translations.literal: Chu kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chu prostrated himself in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 俶中途被足疾，車駕親臨問，令太醫然艾以灸，疾尋愈。

translations.literal: Midway Chu suffered foot ailment; the imperial carriage came in person to inquire and ordered the imperial physician to apply moxibustion; the illness soon healed.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he fell ill in the feet; the emperor visited him in person and had the court physician apply moxa; he soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 還京策勳，宰相進擬加食邑萬戶、實封千戶。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital to record merit the chief ministers proposed adding ten thousand households to his fief income and one thousand to his actual enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, when rewards were tallied the council proposed ten thousand added fief households and one thousand actual enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 上即改白麻，倍加食邑二萬戶、實封二千戶。

translations.literal: The emperor at once revised the white hemp draft, doubling it to twenty thousand fief households and two thousand actual enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor revised the draft himself, doubling it to twenty thousand fief households and two thousand actual enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，俶被病，上臨問，賜白金萬兩、錢千萬、絹萬匹、金器千兩，賜其子惟濬、惟治白金各萬兩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year Chu fell ill; the emperor visited him and granted ten thousand taels of white gold, ten million cash, ten thousand bolts of silk, and one thousand taels of gold vessels, and to his sons Wei Jun and Wei Zhi ten thousand taels of white gold each.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, eighth month, when Chu was ill the emperor visited him with ten thousand taels of white gold, ten million cash, ten thousand bolts of silk, and a thousand taels of goldware, and ten thousand taels each to Wei Jun and Wei Zhi.

sentences.zh: 是冬，車駕幸大名府，詔俶乘肩輿即路。

translations.literal: That winter when the imperial carriage visited Daming Prefecture an edict ordered Chu to travel by sedan chair on the road.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the court went to Daming, Chu was ordered to travel by sedan.

sentences.zh: 六年，又被病，賜告久之，上遣中使賜俶文楸棋局、水精棋子，乃諭旨曰：「朕機務之餘，頗曾留意，以卿在假，可用此遣日。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year he fell ill again and was granted long leave; the emperor sent a palace envoy with a wenqiu chessboard and crystal chess pieces and a message: "In my spare moments from state affairs I have taken some interest in this—since you are on leave you may use it to pass the days."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, ill again, he received extended leave; an envoy brought a wenqiu board and crystal pieces with the message, "I have lately taken up this game in my spare hours—use it to pass your leave."

sentences.zh: 八年十二月，上言曰：「臣以蕞爾之軀，蒙被恩寵，賦祿百萬，兼職數四。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year he memorialized, "Your subject, with this paltry body, has been showered with favor, receiving a salary of a million and holding several offices at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, twelfth month, he wrote, "With my slight person I have been heaped with grace—a salary of a million and four offices at once.

sentences.zh: 元帥之任實本於兵權，國王之號蓋屏於帝室，尚書總百揆之重，中書掌八柄之繁，維師冠於上台，開府當於極品，臣之孱瑣，罔克負荷。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal's post truly rests on military authority; the title of king screens the imperial house; the Director of the Secretariat bears the weight of all ministries; the Secretariat controls the eight powers; Grand Preceptor crowns the upper terrace; Grand Tutor ranks at the highest grade—your subject's meanness cannot bear the load.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal rests on real military power; king shields the throne; Director of the Secretariat heads all ministries; Secretariat wields the eight powers; Grand Preceptor tops the upper ranks; Grand Tutor stands at the highest grade—I am too small to bear them.

sentences.zh: 邦國之制式著等威，名器之間固有涯分，徒速罪戾，以取顛隮。

translations.literal: State institutions display ranks of dignity; titles and regalia have their proper bounds—only to hasten guilt and invite ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks and regalia have fixed limits; to overstep them is only to invite guilt and downfall.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖旨特從省罷。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg that the sacred edict specially grant their abolition."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to abolish them."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 表三上，下詔曰：「 分茅胙土，所以彰世及之榮；

translations.literal: He memorialized three times; an edict said, "Dividing feudal fields and sacrificial lands displays the glory of succession through generations.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials an edict read, "Feudal fields and sacrificial lands honor a line that passes from father to son.

sentences.zh: 大輅繁纓，所以表名器之重。

translations.literal: The great carriage and multiple tassels display the weight of honored titles.
translations.idiomatic: Grand carriage and many tassels show how heavy honored names are.

sentences.zh: 至若褒寵勳德，度越典常，谘於舊章，爰推異數。

translations.literal: To reward meritorious virtue and exceed the regular statutes, consult the old regulations and extend exceptional numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When rewarding merit beyond ordinary statute, the ancients' rules justify exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 乃有體好謙之德，形固讓之辭，敦諭再三，確乎不拔，用曲至公之論，式光知止之風。

translations.literal: Yet there are those whose nature loves humility and whose words show firm declination; exhorted again and again, they are resolute and unmoved—using the utmost public reasoning to glorify the wind of knowing when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some love humility and refuse in earnest; exhorted repeatedly they will not yield—so the court uses utmost fairness to honor the wisdom of stopping in time.

sentences.zh: 淮海國王錢俶方嶽炳靈，風雲通感，奄有勾吳之地，不忘象魏之心。

translations.literal: King Qian Chu of Huaihai: his region shines with spiritual power, wind and cloud answer him; he long held Gouwu lands yet never forgot the imperial capital.
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Chu of Huaihai: his domain gleams with fortune, heaven and earth respond; though he held Gouwu he never forgot the throne.

sentences.zh: 掃境來朝，舉宗宿衛，籍其土宇，入於朝廷，式昭職員，胙之淮海，居天子二老之任，啟真王萬戶之封，並加寵章，用答忠順。

translations.literal: He swept his borders to come to court, brought his clan to guard the capital, surrendered his lands to the court, and was enfeoffed in Huaihai with the duties of the Son of Heaven's two elders and a true king's ten-thousand-household fief—all honors added to answer his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared his realm and came to court, lodged his clan at the capital, gave his lands to the state, and was enfeoffed in Huaihai with an elder's charge and a true king's ten-thousand-household fief—every honor to repay his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而乃屢形表疏，願避官榮，發於深衷，誠不可奪。

translations.literal: Yet again and again in memorials he sought to avoid official glory, speaking from the depths of his heart—truly it cannot be denied.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he asked to lay down rank, speaking from the heart—and this could not be refused.

sentences.zh: 若以靈台偃伯，武庫橐兵，天下一家書軌之無外，五侯九伯征伐之不行。

translations.literal: If the Spirit Terrace rests its hegemon and the armory sheathes its weapons, all under heaven is one family and writing and cart tracks know no outer bounds; the five marquises and nine earls no longer campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With weapons stilled and the realm one, script and roads have no border; the old rights of the five marquises and nine earls to campaign no longer apply.

sentences.zh: 願寢元帥之名，勉徇由衷之請。

translations.literal: Let the name of Grand Marshal sleep, and grant his heartfelt request.
translations.idiomatic: Let the title Grand Marshal be set aside, as he earnestly asks.

sentences.zh: 其乃世祚明德，存於帶礪之盟；

translations.literal: Thus the virtue of his line endures in the covenant sworn with stones and ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Let his house's merit live on in the covenant bound by stone and iron.

sentences.zh: 帝齎良弼，寵以台輔之任。

translations.literal: The emperor cherishes worthy assistants and favors them with posts at the highest council.
translations.idiomatic: The throne treasures good ministers and honors them with the highest council.

sentences.zh: 極馭貴之爵，增衍食之封，非足酬庸，適以昭德，勉膺渥澤，克副眷懷。

translations.literal: The most exalted rank and increased enfeoffment are not enough to repay his service but only to display his virtue—accept this rich grace and fulfill our regard.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme rank and added fiefs cannot repay him but only show his virtue—accept this bounty and meet our hopes.

sentences.zh: 可罷天下兵馬大元帥，餘如故。」

translations.literal: The post of Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven is abolished; all else remains as before."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal of All Armies is abolished; all else stands."

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，改封漢南國王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi he was re-created King of Hannan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 1 he was made King of Hannan.

sentences.zh: 四年春，出為武勝軍節度，改封南陽國王。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he went out as military commissioner of the Wusheng army and was re-created King of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, spring, he became Wusheng military commissioner and was made King of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 俶久被病，詔免入辭。

translations.literal: Chu had long been ill; an edict excused him from farewell audience.
translations.idiomatic: Long ill, he was excused from a farewell audience.

sentences.zh: 將發，賜玉束帶、金唾壺、碗盎等。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart he was granted a jade belt, gold spittoon, bowls, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On departure he received a jade belt, gold spittoon, bowls, and similar gifts.

sentences.zh: 俶四上表讓國王，改封許王。

translations.literal: Chu memorialized four times to decline the title of king and was re-created Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Four times he declined the kingship and was made Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年春，徙封鄧王。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Duangong he was transferred and created Prince of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 1, spring, he was made Prince of Deng.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣使賜生辰器幣，與使者宴飲至幕，有大流星墮正寢前，光燭一庭，是夕暴卒，年六十。

translations.literal: When the court sent envoys with birthday gifts and vessels, he feasted the envoys in his tent until evening; a great meteor fell before the main hall, lighting the whole courtyard, and that night he died suddenly at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: As court envoys came with birthday gifts and he feasted them into the evening, a great meteor fell before his hall, lighting the courtyard; that night he died suddenly, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 俶以天成四年八月二十四日生，至是八月二十四日卒，復與父元瓘卒日同，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Chu was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month in the fourth year of Tiancheng and died on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month at the age of sixty—the same day on which his father Yuan Guan had died; all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Born on the eighth month's twenty-fourth day in Tiancheng 4, he died on the same calendar day at sixty—the very day his father Yuan Guan had died; people marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 上為廢朝七日，追封秦國王，諡忠懿，仍正衙備禮發冊曰：

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court for seven days, posthumously created him Prince of Qin with the posthumous name Loyal and Gracious, and in the main hall with full rites issued the patent:
translations.idiomatic: The court mourned seven days, posthumously created him Prince of Qin with the posthumous name Loyal and Gracious, and in the main hall issued the patent:

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：昊穹眷祐，賢哲挺生，稟象緯之純精，負經綸之盛業，作民父母，為國翰垣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: Heaven favors and assists; the worthy and sage arise, embodying the pure essence of the constellations and bearing the great enterprise of statecraft, as fathers and mothers to the people and pillars of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: Heaven blesses the worthy who arise, bearing the stars' pure essence and the state's great work, as parents to the people and pillars of the realm.

sentences.zh: 其存也冠中台而長諸侯，其沒也峻徽章而崇禮命。

translations.literal: In life they head the central terrace and lead the feudatories; in death lofty titles and honored rites exalt them.
translations.idiomatic: Living, they head the central ministries and lead the princes; dead, exalted titles and grand rites honor them.

sentences.zh: 谘爾故安時鎮國崇文耀武宣德守道功臣、武勝軍節度、鄧州管內觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司、守太師、尚書令兼中書令、使持節鄧州諸軍事、行鄧州刺史、上柱國、鄧王、食邑九萬七千戶、食實封一萬六千九百戶、賜劍履上殿、詔書不名錢俶，嗣祖考之令德，奠東南之奧區，開國承家，本仁祖義；

translations.literal: To you, the late Merit Subject Who Pacifies the State, Honors Culture, Displays Martial Glory, Extends Virtue, and Guards the Way, Wusheng military commissioner, observation and disposition commissioner of Dengzhou, Grand Preceptor with Grand Tutor honors, Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Commissioner with full powers over Dengzhou military affairs, acting prefect of Deng, Upper Pillar of State, Prince of Deng, fief of ninety-seven thousand households with sixteen thousand nine hundred actual enfeoffment, granted sword and shoes in the palace and omission from edicts—Qian Chu: you inherited your ancestors' fine virtue and settled the rich southeast, founding a state and continuing the house in benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: To the late Qian Chu—merit subject, Wusheng commissioner, Dengzhou commissioner, Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Deng with ninety-seven thousand fief households, sword and shoes in the palace, unnamed in edicts—you inherited ancestral virtue and ruled the southeast, founding a house in benevolence and righteousness:

sentences.zh: 以忠孝而保社稷，以廉讓而化人民；

translations.literal: By loyalty and filial piety you preserved the altars of soil and grain; by integrity and yielding you transformed the people.
translations.idiomatic: By loyalty and filial piety you guarded the realm; by modesty you transformed your people.

sentences.zh: 勤翊戴於累朝，克惠綏於一境，世傳威略，誌慕聲明。

translations.literal: Through many dynasties you diligently supported the throne and brought gentle rule to one region; your house transmitted martial renown and your will sought a bright name.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive courts you aided the throne and soothed one region; your line kept martial fame and your heart sought renown.

sentences.zh: 當武庫戢兵，洞閱詩書之府；

translations.literal: When the armory sheathed its weapons you opened the storehouse of poetry and books.
translations.idiomatic: When arms were stilled you turned to the halls of poetry and learning.

sentences.zh: 洎秣陵問罪，雄張犄角之師。

translations.literal: When Moling was punished you boldly deployed horn-like armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling was chastised you sent armies like pincers.

sentences.zh: 致區宇之同文，賴忠良之協力。

translations.literal: The realm was united in one script, relying on loyal ministers' combined strength.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was unified in writing, thanks to loyal ministers working together.

sentences.zh: 逮於纂紹，益享崇高，蘊明哲而保身，務傾輸而竭節，盡獻土壤，來歸闕庭，予嘉乃功，薦錫殊寵。

translations.literal: On succeeding to rule you enjoyed still higher honor, harboring wisdom to preserve yourself and pouring out your utmost loyalty, surrendering all lands and coming to the palace gate; I praised your merit and heaped special favor upon you.
translations.idiomatic: On succeeding you rose higher still, wise enough to preserve yourself and loyal to the end, giving up your soil and coming to court; I praised your service and granted exceptional grace.

sentences.zh: 而道隆簡退，誌尚謙衝，屢辭卻縠之權，難奪範宣之讓。

translations.literal: Yet your way was lofty and retiring, your will humble; again and again you declined the authority of Gu and the yielding of Fan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you loved simplicity and humility, repeatedly declining command as Gu did and yielding as Fan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 朕深惟勳舊，俾就養頤，爰出殿於大邦，庶聿臻於眉壽，式繄元老，永輔眇躬。

translations.literal: I deeply considered your long service and sent you to a great state to nurture your years, hoping you would reach old age; you were an elder forever to aid my slight person.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of your long service I sent you to a great domain to rest, hoping for long life; you were an elder to support my humble self.

sentences.zh: 何天道之難諶，而梁木之斯壞！

translations.literal: How hard to fathom Heaven's way—and now the ridgepole is broken!
translations.idiomatic: How inscrutable is Heaven's way—the great beam is fallen!

sentences.zh: 長沙既往，空存甲令之勳；

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha is gone, leaving only the merit recorded in the ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha is gone, leaving only ordinances of merit.

sentences.zh: 征虜雲亡，但見雲台之像。

translations.literal: The Pacifying General has perished in the clouds, leaving only his image on the Cloud Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacifying General has vanished, leaving only his portrait on the Cloud Terrace.

sentences.zh: 賵賻從於異等，嗟悼廢於臨朝；

translations.literal: Funeral gifts follow an exceptional grade; lamentation halts the court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts are of the highest grade; the court mourns in session.

sentences.zh: 寧酬柱石之勳，未極君臣之分。

translations.literal: How can pillar-and-stone merit be repaid? The bond between ruler and minister is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar merit cannot be fully repaid; ruler and minister have not yet reached the end of their bond.

sentences.zh: 庸加典則，以厚始終。

translations.literal: Let canonical rites be added to thicken the beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Let canonical honors thicken beginning and end.

sentences.zh: 今遣使太中大夫、尚書工部侍郎、上柱國、汾陽郡開國侯、食邑一千戶、賜紫金魚袋郭贄持節冊贈爾為秦國王。

translations.literal: Now Grand Master of the Palace, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works, Upper Pillar of State, Marquis of Fenyang with a fief of one thousand households, granted the purple-gold fish bag—Guo Zan—is sent with credentials to posthumously create you Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Guo Zan is sent with credentials to posthumously create you Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 德無不報，予敢忘於格言；

translations.literal: Virtue is never unrewarded—I dare not forget the ancient saying.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue is never unrewarded—I dare not forget the maxim.

sentences.zh: 魂而有知，爾尚欽於天命。

translations.literal: If your soul has awareness, still revere Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: If your spirit knows, still honor Heaven's command.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 命中使護其喪歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: The court ordered envoys to escort the coffin home for burial in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were ordered to escort the coffin for burial in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自鏐至俶世有吳越之地僅百年，管內諸州皆子弟，將校授任而後請命於朝，有至使相者。

translations.literal: From Liu to Chu the house held Wu and Yue for barely a hundred years; every prefecture within their domain was held by sons and younger brothers, and commanders were appointed locally before requesting confirmation from court—some rose to chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: From Qian Liu to Chu the clan held Wu-Yue barely a century; every prefecture was held by kin, officers appointed locally then confirmed at court—some reached chancellor.

sentences.zh: 俶任太師、尚書令兼中書令四十年，為元帥三十五年。

translations.literal: Chu held the posts of Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat for forty years and was Grand Marshal for thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat for forty years and Grand Marshal for thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 及歸朝卒，子惟演、惟濟皆童年，召見慰勞，並起家諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: When he returned to court and died, his sons Wei Yan and Wei Ji were still children; summoned and comforted, both began their careers as generals of the imperial guards.
translations.idiomatic: After he came to court and died, sons Wei Yan and Wei Ji were still boys; the emperor summoned and comforted them and both began as guards generals.

sentences.zh: 善始令終，窮極富貴，福履之盛，近代無比。

translations.literal: A good beginning and good end, wealth and honor to the utmost—such fortune in recent times has had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: From fine start to fine end, wealth and honor at their peak—no parallel in recent times.

sentences.zh: 然甚儉素，自奉尤薄，常服大帛之衣，幃帳茵褥皆用紫絁，食不重味。

translations.literal: Yet he was very frugal and plain; his personal upkeep was especially spare—he regularly wore coarse silk, curtains and bedding all of purple twill, and his food had no duplicate flavors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was deeply frugal: coarse silk for daily dress, purple twill for curtains and bedding, never two dishes at a meal.

sentences.zh: 頗知書，雅好吟詠。

translations.literal: He was quite learned and fond of composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was well read and loved to write verse.

sentences.zh: 在吳越日，自編其詩數百首為《正本集》，因陶穀奉使至杭州，求為之序。

translations.literal: In Wuyue days he compiled several hundred of his poems into the Corrected Collection and, when Tao Gu came on mission to Hangzhou, asked him to write a preface.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuyue he gathered several hundred poems into the Corrected Collection and asked Tao Gu, on mission to Hangzhou, for a preface.

sentences.zh: 性謙和，未嘗忤物。

translations.literal: His nature was modest and yielding; he never gave offense.
translations.idiomatic: Humble by nature, he never gave offense.

sentences.zh: 在藩日，每朝廷使至，接遇勤厚。

translations.literal: While still in his domain, whenever court envoys arrived he received them with diligent warmth.
translations.idiomatic: In his realm he always received court envoys with warm diligence.

sentences.zh: 所上乘輿、服物、器玩，製作精妙，每遣使修貢，必羅列於庭，焚香再拜，其恭謹如此。

translations.literal: Carriages, garments, vessels, and curios he presented were exquisitely made; whenever he sent tribute he arrayed them in the courtyard, burned incense, and bowed twice—such was his reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The carriages, robes, and curios he sent were finely made; each tribute he lined in the court, burned incense, and bowed twice—so reverent was he.

sentences.zh: 崇信釋氏，前後造寺數百，歸朝又以愛子為僧。

translations.literal: He revered Buddhism and built hundreds of temples; after coming to court he also made a beloved son a monk.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Buddhism, building hundreds of temples; in court he also tonsured a beloved son.

sentences.zh: 善草書，上一日遣使謂曰：「聞卿善草聖，可寫一二紙進來。」

translations.literal: Skilled in cursive script, one day the emperor sent word: "I hear you excel at cursive—write a sheet or two and send them in."
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in cursive, the emperor once said, "I hear you are a master of cursive—send a few sheets."

sentences.zh: 俶即以舊所書絹圖上之，詔書褒美，因賜玉硯金匣一，紅綠象牙管筆、龍鳳墨、蜀箋、盈丈紙皆百數。

translations.literal: Chu at once sent up silk with his old writings; an edict praised him and granted a jade inkstone in a gold case, red and green ivory brushes, dragon-and-phoenix ink, Shu paper, and paper a zhang in size—a hundred of each.
translations.idiomatic: He sent old writings on silk; the court praised him and gave a jade inkstone in a gold case, ivory brushes, imperial ink, Shu paper, and full-length sheets—a hundred each.

sentences.zh: 屬久病家居，有黃門趙海被酒造其第求見，因出藥數丸謂俶曰：「此頗療目疾，願王即餌之。」

translations.literal: While long ill at home, the Yellow Gate attendant Zhao Hai came drunk to his residence seeking audience and produced several pills, saying to Chu, "These greatly treat eye ailments—my lord should take them at once."
translations.idiomatic: Long ill at home, Yellow Gate attendant Zhao Hai came drunk and offered several pills, saying, "These cure eye disease—take them now."

sentences.zh: 俶即餌焉。

translations.literal: Chu took them at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chu swallowed them immediately.

sentences.zh: 既去，家人皆惶駭不測，俶曰：「此但醉耳，又何疑哉？」

translations.literal: After he left the household was terrified and uncertain; Chu said, "He was only drunk—why doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: When he left the household was alarmed; Chu said, "He was merely drunk—why worry?"

sentences.zh: 後數日，上聞大驚，捕海係獄，決杖流海島。

translations.literal: Several days later when the emperor heard of it he was greatly shocked, arrested Hai and imprisoned him, and sentenced him to beating and exile to a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the emperor was shocked, seized Hai, beat him, and exiled him to an island.

sentences.zh: 初，俶為胡進思所立，廢其兄倧，徙越州，資給豐厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chu was installed by Hu Jinsi he deposed his elder brother Cong and moved him to Yuezhou with rich provision.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Jinsi installed Chu he deposed his brother Cong to Yuezhou with generous support.

sentences.zh: 進思屢請除之，恐為後患，俶泣曰：「若殺吾兄，吾終不忍，汝欲行其志，吾當退避賢路。」

translations.literal: Jinsi repeatedly asked to have him removed, fearing future trouble; Chu wept and said, "If you kill my elder brother I could never bear it—if you wish to carry out your will, I will yield the path of worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi repeatedly urged killing Cong, fearing future trouble; Chu wept, "Kill my brother and I cannot bear it—do as you will, and I will step aside."

sentences.zh: 進思慚而退。

translations.literal: Jinsi withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Jinsi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俶慮進思害倧，遣親將薛溫為倧守衛，戒之曰：「委汝以保全廢王，苟有非常，汝當以死捍之。」
