translations.literal: Chu feared Jinsi would harm Cong and sent his trusted general Xue Wen to guard him, admonishing him, "I entrust you to preserve the deposed king; if anything untoward occurs you must die defending him."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jinsi would harm Cong, Chu sent Xue Wen to guard him with the charge, "Keep the deposed king safe—if danger comes, die defending him."

sentences.zh: 溫至越旬餘，有二卒夜持刃逾垣入，倧闔戶拒之，呼聲達於外，溫領徒而入，斃二卒於庭中，乃進思之所遣也。

translations.literal: Wen reached Yue after more than ten days when two soldiers at night scaled the wall with blades; Cong shut his door against them and his cries reached outside; Wen led his men in and killed the two in the courtyard—they had been sent by Jinsi.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days in Yue two soldiers climbed the wall by night; Cong barred his door and shouted; Wen rushed in and killed them in the court—they were Jinsi's men.

sentences.zh: 進思因憂懼，疽發背，卒。

translations.literal: Jinsi, gripped by worry and fear, developed a carbuncle on his back and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi, anxious and afraid, developed a back carbuncle and died.

sentences.zh: 從左右屢有以倧為言，叔終拒之。

translations.literal: Those around him often spoke of Cong, but Chu always refused.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants often urged action against Cong, but Chu always refused.

sentences.zh: 倧居越州二十餘年卒。

translations.literal: Cong lived at Yuezhou more than twenty years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Cong dwelt at Yuezhou over twenty years and died.

sentences.zh: 俶自建隆已來貢奉不絕，及用兵江左，所貢數十倍。

translations.literal: From Jianlong onward Chu's tribute never ceased, and during the Jiangzuo campaign his gifts were several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianlong on his tribute never stopped; during the lower Yangzi war it multiplied tenfold.

sentences.zh: 先是鏐與戰士多賜己姓，後俶歸朝，皆稱同宗。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu had given many warriors his surname; after Chu came to court they all claimed kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had given many soldiers his surname; after Chu submitted to court they all called themselves kin.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，詔令復本姓。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua an edict ordered restoration of their original surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3 an edict restored their original surnames.

sentences.zh: 又浙中劉氏避鏐諱，改為金氏，亦令還故。

translations.literal: In Zhe the Liu clan had changed to Jin to avoid Liu's taboo; they too were ordered back to their former name.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhe the Liu clan had become Jin to avoid Qian Liu's taboo; they too were restored.

sentences.zh: 景德中，有司請以禮賢宅為司天監，真宗以先朝所賜，不許。

translations.literal: In Jingde the authorities asked to make the Estate for Honoring the Worthy the Directorate of Astronomy; Zhenzong, because it was a gift of the former court, refused.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde officials proposed turning the Estate for Honoring the Worthy into the Directorate of Astronomy; Zhenzong refused, as it was a former gift.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，子惟演等復表上之，詔賜錢五萬貫，仍各賜第一區。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu sons Wei Yan and others again memorialized to surrender it; an edict granted fifty thousand strings of cash and each a first-rank residence.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 8 sons Wei Yan and others again offered the estate; the court granted fifty thousand strings of cash and each a top residence.

sentences.zh: 子惟濬、惟治、惟渲、惟演、惟灝、惟溍、惟濟。

translations.literal: His sons were Wei Jun, Wei Zhi, Wei Xuan, Wei Yan, Wei Hao, Wei Jin, and Wei Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His sons: Wei Jun, Wei Zhi, Wei Xuan, Wei Yan, Wei Hao, Wei Jin, and Wei Ji.

sentences.zh: 惟渲至韶州團練使，惟灝賀州團練使，惟溍至左龍武將軍、獎州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei Xuan rose to regimental commander of Shaozhou; Wei Hao regimental commander of Hezhou; Wei Jin to Left Dragon Martial General and prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuan reached regimental commander of Shaozhou; Wei Hao of Hezhou; Wei Jin Left Dragon Martial General and prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 惟演自有傳。

translations.literal: Wei Yan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子 惟濬

translations.literal: Son: Wei Jun
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wei Jun

sentences.zh: 惟濬字禹川，俶嫡子也。

translations.literal: Wei Jun, courtesy name Yuchuan, was Chu's legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun, courtesy name Yuchuan, was Chu's heir.

sentences.zh: 裁數歲，俶表授鎮海鎮東兩軍節度副大使、檢校太保、鈐轄兩浙管內土客諸軍事。

translations.literal: When only a few years old Chu memorialized appointing him vice military commissioner of the Zhenhai and Zhendong armies, acting Grand Guardian, and commander of all military affairs of native and guest troops in the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: As a child Chu had him appointed vice commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, acting Grand Guardian, and commander of Zhe military affairs.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong he was promoted to acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 1 he was made acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 三年，領建武軍節度。

translations.literal: In the third year he took charge of the Jianwu army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he headed the Jianwu circuit.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he became acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，來朝，因侍祠南郊。

translations.literal: That winter he came to court and attended the southern suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he came to court for the southern suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，復來朝，侍郊祀，命兵部員外郎、知制誥盧多遜迎勞之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he came again to attend the suburban sacrifice; Vice Minister of War and Edict Drafter Lu Duosun was sent to welcome and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he returned for the suburban rites; Lu Duosun was sent to receive him.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，授鎮東等軍節度、浙江東西道觀察處置、兩浙製置營田發運等使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was appointed military commissioner of Zhendong and the like, observation and disposition commissioner of the Zhe east and west routes, and commissioner for Zhe military farms and transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 he became Zhendong commissioner, Zhe observation commissioner, and transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，來朝，太祖召宴苑中，令黃門奏《簫韶》樂，與諸王同席而坐。

translations.literal: Before long he came to court; Taizu summoned him to feast in the garden, had the Yellow Gate perform the Xiaoshao music, and seated him with the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he came to court; Taizu feasted him in the garden, had the Xiaoshao played, and seated him with the princes.

sentences.zh: 賜白玉帶、珠綴衣、水精鞍勒御馬，賜賚钜萬計。

translations.literal: He was granted a white jade belt, pearl-trimmed robe, crystal saddle and bridle with imperial horse, and gifts worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He received a white jade belt, pearl robe, crystal-bridled horse, and gifts worth a fortune.

sentences.zh: 月餘遣歸，辭日，又賜襲衣、玉帶、金鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was sent home; on his farewell day he was again granted court robes, jade belt, and gold saddle and bridle with horse.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he left; on farewell day he received court dress, jade belt, and gold-bridled horse.

sentences.zh: 四年，又來朝，因侍祠南郊，寵待殊等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he came again to attend the southern suburban sacrifice and was favored exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he came again for the southern rites with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 及大兵征金陵，惟濬從父下毗陵，以功加平章事。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Jinling Wei Jun followed his father to take Piling and for merit was promoted to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinling campaign he followed his father to Piling and was made Grand Councilor for merit.

sentences.zh: 九年，隨俶入朝，俶先歸，留惟濬扈從郊祀西洛。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Chu to court; Chu returned first and left Wei Jun to attend the western capital suburban rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he followed Chu to court; Chu went home first, leaving Wei Jun for the western capital rites.

sentences.zh: 惟濬與俶諸子共進錢金、綾羅、犀玉帶笏、犀角、象牙、丁香、金玉馬腦鞍勒、金玉珠翠首飾、樂器、博具、器皿什物、馬橐駝牛驢車凡數十萬計。

translations.literal: Wei Jun together with Chu's sons jointly presented cash, gold, silk gauze, rhinoceros jade belts and tablets, rhinoceros horn, ivory, cloves, gold and jade agate saddles and bridles, gold and jade pearl and kingfisher headdresses, musical instruments, gaming sets, vessels and goods, and horses, camels, oxen, donkeys, and carts numbering several hundred thousand items.
translations.idiomatic: He and Chu's sons presented cash, gold, silks, rhinoceros and jade regalia, incense, saddles, jewelry, instruments, vessels, and livestock by the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 俶妻俞氏又進金銀十餘萬、犀二十株、通犀赬犀玉帶二十二條、水晶佛像十二事。

translations.literal: Chu's wife Lady Yu also presented more than one hundred thousand in gold and silver, twenty rhinoceros horns, twenty-two rhinoceros jade belts, and twelve crystal Buddha images.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu also sent over one hundred thousand in gold and silver, twenty horns, twenty-two rhinoceros jade belts, and twelve crystal Buddhas.

sentences.zh: 惟濬又進女樂十人，上不納，各賜錦彩三十段遣還之。

translations.literal: Wei Jun also presented ten female musicians; the emperor did not accept them and each was granted thirty bolts of brocade and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent ten female musicians; the emperor declined and gave each thirty bolts of brocade to return home.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，杭州以錢氏家廟所藏唐、梁以來累朝所賜玉冊竹冊各三副、鐵券一來上，上悉以賜惟濬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua Hangzhou presented from the Qian clan ancestral temple three sets each of jade books and bamboo books bestowed by the Tang and Liang and one iron certificate; the emperor gave them all to Wei Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In early Chunhua Hangzhou sent from the clan temple three jade and three bamboo registers from Tang and Liang and an iron certificate; all were given to Wei Jun.

sentences.zh: 明年春，得疾暴卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: The next spring he fell suddenly ill and died at the age of thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring he fell ill and died suddenly at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 廢朝二日，追封邠王，諡安僖，中使典喪事。

translations.literal: Court was suspended two days; he was posthumously created Prince of Bin with posthumous name Peaceful and Lamented, and a palace envoy directed the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned two days; he was posthumously made Prince of Bin, Peaceful and Lamented, with a palace envoy overseeing rites.

sentences.zh: 子守吉、守讓。

translations.literal: Sons Shouji and Shourang.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Shouji and Shourang.

sentences.zh: 守吉至西京作坊使。

translations.literal: Shouji rose to commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Shouji became commissioner of the Western Capital workshops.

sentences.zh: 守讓字希仲，以蔭累遷供備庫使，天禧四年，錄諸國之後，加領榮州刺史，改東染院使，卒。

translations.literal: Shourang, courtesy name Xizhong, by yin privilege rose to commissioner of the supply depot; in the fourth year of Tianxi, when recording descendants of various states, he was additionally made prefect of Rong and changed to commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Office, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Shourang, courtesy name Xizhong, rose by yin privilege to supply commissioner; in Tianxi 4 he was made prefect of Rong and later Eastern Dyeing commissioner, then died.

sentences.zh: 守讓頗勤學為文章，退居多閉關讀書，屢獻歌頌，真宗優詔褒獎。

translations.literal: Shourang studied diligently and wrote essays; in retirement he often shut his doors to read and repeatedly presented odes and hymns; Zhenzong issued gracious edicts praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Shourang studied hard and wrote well; in retirement he read behind closed doors and often sent poems; Zhenzong praised him in edict.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子恕，娶曹王元偁女長安縣主。

translations.literal: Son Shu married the Princess of Chang'an, daughter of Prince of Cao Yuan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu married Princess Chang'an, daughter of Prince of Cao Yuan Zheng.

sentences.zh: 子 惟治

translations.literal: Son: Wei Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wei Zhi

sentences.zh: 惟治字和世，廢王倧之長子。

translations.literal: Wei Zhi, courtesy name Heshi, was the eldest son of the deposed king Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhi, courtesy name Heshi, was deposed king Cong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 倧初遷於越而惟治生，俶愛之，養為己子。

translations.literal: When Cong was first moved to Yue, Wei Zhi was born; Chu loved him and raised him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Born when Cong was sent to Yue, he was loved by Chu and raised as a son.

sentences.zh: 幼好讀書。

translations.literal: From youth he loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books from childhood.

sentences.zh: 八歲授兩浙牙內諸軍指揮使，判軍糧營田事，又改德化軍使，遷檢校太保、台州團練使。

translations.literal: At eight he was appointed commander of the Zhe internal guard, judged military grain and farm affairs, then changed to commissioner of the Dehua army, promoted acting Grand Guardian and regimental commander of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he commanded the Zhe guard, managed grain and farms, became Dehua commissioner, then acting Grand Guardian and Taizhou regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年四月，製授寧遠軍節度、檢校太傅，仍兼衙職，與惟濬節旄同日而至，國人榮之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Qiande he was formally appointed military commissioner of the Ningyuan army and acting Grand Tutor, still holding palace office; his commission arrived the same day as Wei Jun's—a glory for the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 4, fourth month, he was made Ningyuan commissioner and acting Grand Tutor; his commission arrived the same day as Wei Jun's, to the people's joy.

sentences.zh: 王師討江南，惟治從俶率兵下常州，策勳改奉國軍節度。

translations.literal: When the imperial army chastised Jiangnan Wei Zhi followed Chu to take Changzhou; for merit he was changed to military commissioner of the Fengguo army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan campaign he followed Chu to Changzhou and was made Fengguo commissioner for merit.

sentences.zh: 俶入朝，命惟治權發遣軍國事。

translations.literal: When Chu came to court he was ordered to act in dispatching state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu went to court Wei Zhi was left to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 俶還，令奉幣入貢，撫諭命賜甚厚。

translations.literal: When Chu returned he was ordered to present tribute with ritual gifts; the court's grants and comfort were very rich.
translations.idiomatic: On Chu's return he bore tribute gifts and received lavish court rewards.

sentences.zh: 惟治又獻塗金銀香師子、香鹿鳳鶴孔雀、寶裝髹合、扣金瓷器萬事，吳繚綾千匹。

translations.literal: Wei Zhi also presented gilt-silver incense lions, deer, phoenixes, cranes, and peacocks, treasure-mounted lacquer boxes, gold-mounted porcelain ten thousand items, and a thousand bolts of Wu gauze.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent gilt incense beasts, lacquer boxes, ten thousand gold-mounted porcelains, and a thousand bolts of Wu silk.

sentences.zh: 辭日，賜襲衣玉帶、塗金鞍勒馬、金銀器、繒彩逾萬計。

translations.literal: On his farewell day he was granted court robes, jade belt, gilt saddle and bridle with horse, gold and silver vessels, and silks exceeding ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving he received court dress, jade belt, gilt horse, gold and silverware, and over ten thousand in silks.

sentences.zh: 太宗嗣位，進檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded he was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he became acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，俶再入覲，又權國事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo Chu came again to court and once more acted in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 3, when Chu came again, Wei Zhi again governed the realm.

sentences.zh: 一夕廄中火，惟治率兵臨高下視，令親信十數輩仗劍申令，敢後顧者斬，頃之火息。

translations.literal: One night a fire broke out in the stables; Wei Zhi led troops to a high place to oversee, ordered a dozen trusted men with swords to proclaim that anyone who looked back would be beheaded, and soon the fire was out.
translations.idiomatic: One night the stables burned; he stood above with swordsmen warning that any who looked back would die, and the fire was soon quenched.

sentences.zh: 妻族有隸帳下者恃親犯法，惟治命杖背於府門。

translations.literal: A kinsman by marriage in his service relied on kinship to break the law; Wei Zhi ordered him flogged at the prefectural gate.
translations.idiomatic: A wife's kinsman in his service broke the law trusting in kinship; Wei Zhi had him beaten at the gate.

sentences.zh: 俶既納土，朝廷命考功郎中範旻知杭州，惟治奉兵民圖籍、帑廩管籥授旻，與其弟惟渲、惟灝歸朝。

translations.literal: After Chu surrendered his territory the court appointed Review-of-Merits Director Fan Min to govern Hangzhou; Wei Zhi delivered troops, people, registers, and treasury keys to Min and returned to court with brothers Wei Xuan and Wei Hao.
translations.idiomatic: After surrender Fan Min was sent to Hangzhou; Wei Zhi handed over troops, registers, and treasury keys and came to court with Wei Xuan and Wei Hao.

sentences.zh: 次近郊，遣內侍護諸司供帳迎勞至京師，即日召對長春殿，賜衣服、金帶、鞍勒馬、器幣，改領鎮國軍節度。

translations.literal: Near the suburbs palace attendants were sent to prepare honors and welcome him to the capital; that day he was received in the Changchun Hall, granted robes, gold belt, saddle and bridle with horse and vessels, and transferred to military commissioner of the Zhenguo army.
translations.idiomatic: Near the capital attendants prepared honors; that day he was received in the Changchun Hall with robes, gold belt, horse, and goods, and made Zhenguo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，車駕幸俶第，召見惟治，賜白金萬兩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year when the imperial carriage visited Chu's residence Wei Zhi was summoned and granted ten thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, eighth month, when the emperor visited Chu, Wei Zhi was summoned and given ten thousand taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 惟治善草隸，尤好二王書，嘗曰：「心能禦手，手能御筆，則法在其中矣。」

translations.literal: Wei Zhi was skilled in cursive and clerical script and especially loved the Two Wangs' calligraphy, often saying, "When the heart can master the hand and the hand can master the brush, then method lies within."
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical script and loved the Two Wangs, saying, "When heart masters hand and hand masters brush, method is within."

sentences.zh: 家藏書帖圖書甚眾，太宗知之，嘗謂近臣曰：「錢俶兒侄多工草書。」

translations.literal: His house held many collected books and rubbings; Taizong knew this and once told close ministers, "Many of Qian Chu's sons and nephews excel at cursive."
translations.idiomatic: His home held many books and rubbings; Taizong said to ministers, "Many of the Qian nephews write fine cursive."

sentences.zh: 因命翰林書學賀丕顯詣其第，遍取視之，曰：「諸錢皆效浙僧亞棲之跡，故筆力軟弱，獨惟治為工耳。」

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Hanlin Calligraphy Scholar He Pixian to go to his residence and examine them all; Pixian said, "All the Qian men imitate the Zhe monk Yaxi's traces, so their brush strength is weak—only Wei Zhi is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hanlin calligrapher He Pixian to review them: "All imitate the monk Yaxi—weak brushwork; only Wei Zhi is skilled."

sentences.zh: 惟治嘗以鍾繇、王羲之、唐玄宗墨跡凡七軸為獻，優詔褒答。

translations.literal: Wei Zhi once presented seven scrolls of ink traces by Zhong Yao, Wang Xizhi, and Emperor Xuanzong of Tang; a gracious edict praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented seven scrolls by Zhong Yao, Wang Xizhi, and Tang Xuanzong; the court praised him in edict.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，大出師征幽州，命惟治知真定軍府兼兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi a great army marched against Youzhou; Wei Zhi was ordered to govern Zhending Prefecture and concurrently serve as commander of all forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, during the great march on Youzhou, he was made prefect of Zhending and commander of forces.

sentences.zh: 前一日曲宴內殿，惟治獻詩，帝覽之悅，酒半，遣小黃門密諭北面之寄。

translations.literal: The day before, at an inner banquet, Wei Zhi presented a poem; the emperor was pleased, and at mid-feast sent a minor Yellow Gate to confide secretly the trust placed in the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The eve before, at an inner feast he presented verse; pleased, the emperor secretly confided the northern trust at mid-banquet.

sentences.zh: 至則訓兵享士，頗勤政務，設廚饌於城門以待使傳。

translations.literal: On arrival he trained troops and feasted soldiers, attended diligently to government, and set kitchens at the gate to await envoys.
translations.idiomatic: There he drilled troops, feasted men, governed diligently, and set kitchens at the gate for messengers.

sentences.zh: 初，惟濬雖俶嫡嗣，然俶以其放蕩無檢，故器惟治，再俾權國務。

translations.literal: Earlier, though Wei Jun was Chu's legitimate heir, Chu because of his dissolute and unrestrained ways favored Wei Zhi and twice entrusted him with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei Jun was heir, Chu favored Wei Zhi for Wei Jun's dissipation and twice left him in charge.

sentences.zh: 嘗一夕俶暴疾，孫妃悉斂符籥付惟治，後惟濬知之，甚恚恨。

translations.literal: Once at night Chu fell suddenly ill; Consort Sun gathered all seals and tallies and gave them to Wei Zhi; later when Wei Jun learned of it he was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: One night Chu fell ill; Lady Sun gave all seals to Wei Zhi; Wei Jun later learned and resented it.

sentences.zh: 洎入朝，惟濬止奉朝請，而委惟治藩任焉。

translations.literal: When he came to court Wei Jun only attended audiences while frontier duties were entrusted to Wei Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: At court Wei Jun only attended audiences; frontier duty went to Wei Zhi.

sentences.zh: 俶薨召還，起復檢校太師。

translations.literal: When Chu died he was recalled; on mourning leave he resumed as acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled at Chu's death, he resumed mourning as acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 移疾就第百日，有司請罷奉，特詔續給。

translations.literal: Ill at home a hundred days, the authorities asked to stop his salary; a special edict continued payment.
translations.idiomatic: Ill at home a hundred days, officials sought to stop salary; a special edict continued it.

sentences.zh: 累上表請罷節鎮，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Repeatedly memorializing to resign his commission, gracious edicts refused.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to resign his command; gracious edicts refused.

sentences.zh: 惟治既病，心恍惚，家事不肅。

translations.literal: Once ill Wei Zhi's mind grew confused and household order lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In illness his mind wandered and his household fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，僮奴以奸私殺人於庭，事連閨閫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping a servant killed someone in the court for illicit relations, the affair touching the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xianping a servant murdered someone in the court over illicit affairs involving the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 真宗為停按鞫，止授右監門衛上將軍，其子駕部員外郎丕責授郢州團練副使。

translations.literal: Zhenzong halted the investigation, only appointing him Right Gate Guard Senior General; his son Vice Director of the Transport Office Pi was demoted to vice regimental commander of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong stopped the inquiry, making him only Right Gate Guard Senior General; son Pi was demoted to Ezhou vice commander.

sentences.zh: 晚年頗貧匱。

translations.literal: In his later years he was quite poor.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he grew poor.

sentences.zh: 景德中，其弟惟演獻文，上對宰相稱其公王之後，能苦心翰墨，令記其名，因曰：「錢氏繼世忠順，子孫可念，如聞惟治頗貧乏，尤可軫惻。」

translations.literal: In Jingde his brother Wei Yan presented a literary work; the emperor told the chief ministers he was of a ducal house, labored at brush and ink, and ordered his name recorded, saying, "The Qian house has been loyal for generations—their descendants merit regard; I hear Wei Zhi is quite impoverished and is especially to be pitied."
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde Wei Yan presented writing; the emperor told ministers the Qian line was loyal and noted Wei Zhi's poverty with pity.

sentences.zh: 特轉右武衛上將軍，月給奉十萬。

translations.literal: He was specially transferred to Right Martial Guard Senior General with a monthly salary of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Martial Guard Senior General with one hundred thousand monthly salary.

sentences.zh: 累加左驍衛上將軍、左神武統軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Flying Cavalry Senior General and Left Divine Martial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Flying Cavalry Senior General and Left Divine Martial Commander.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年七月，卒，年六十六，贈太師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 7, seventh month, he died at sixty-six and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 初，有司援統軍陳承昭、孟玨例，當贈東宮保傅。

translations.literal: At first the authorities, citing Commanders Chen Chengzhao and Meng Jue, proposed posthumous Eastern Palace Guardian and Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Initially officials, citing Chen Chengzhao and Meng Jue, proposed Eastern Palace Guardian and Tutor.

sentences.zh: 上以俶奉土歸國，優其贈典。

translations.literal: The emperor because Chu had surrendered his territory enriched the posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chu had surrendered his lands the emperor enriched the posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 又聞群臣家貧乏者不欲官給喪事，為罷詔葬。

translations.literal: Hearing that poor ministers' families did not wish the court to fund funerals, he canceled the edict-mandated burial.
translations.idiomatic: Learning poor ministers disliked state-funded funerals, he canceled the mandated court burial.

sentences.zh: 錄其四子官，及外弟、子婿、親校並甄擢之。

translations.literal: His four sons were given office, and brothers-in-law, sons-in-law, and trusted officers were all promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons were given office; in-laws, sons-in-law, and officers were promoted.

sentences.zh: 惟治好學，聚圖書萬餘卷，多異本。

translations.literal: Wei Zhi loved learning and gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of books, many rare editions.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and collected over ten thousand scrolls, many rare texts.

sentences.zh: 慕皮、陸為詩，有集十卷。

translations.literal: He admired Pi and Lu as poets and had a collection of ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Pi Rixiu and Lu Guimeng and left ten juan of verse.

sentences.zh: 書跡多為人藏秘，晚年雖病廢，猶或揮翰。

translations.literal: His writing was much hoarded in secret; even in late illness when crippled he sometimes still wielded the brush.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy was widely hoarded; even crippled in old age he sometimes wrote.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗語惟演曰：「朕知惟治工書，然以疾不欲遣使往取，卿為求數輻進來。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong once told Wei Yan, "I know Wei Zhi writes well, but because of illness I do not wish to send envoys to fetch—you seek several sheets and present them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong told Wei Yan, "I know Wei Zhi writes well but will not send for it because of his illness—you bring me several sheets."

sentences.zh: 翌日，寫聖製詩數十章以獻，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: The next day he copied several dozen imperial poems and presented them and was granted one thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he copied dozens of imperial poems and was given a thousand taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 初鎮四明，嘗夢神人披甲，自稱「西嶽神」，謂惟治曰：「公面有缺文」，即捧土培之。

translations.literal: When he first governed Siming he dreamed of a man in armor who called himself Spirit of the Western Peak and said to Wei Zhi, "Your face has a missing mark," and at once piled earth to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Governing Siming he dreamed an armored man, the Western Peak god, said his face lacked a mark and mounded earth to repair it.

sentences.zh: 後領華州節鉞二十年。

translations.literal: Later he held the Huazhou commission for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He later held Huazhou command for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 子丕字簡之，幼好學。

translations.literal: Son Pi, courtesy name Jianzhi, loved learning from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Son Pi, courtesy name Jianzhi, loved learning young.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，俶上言欲求舉進士，太宗以其世家子，特召試內署，授秘書丞，賜金紫，累遷駕部郎中。

translations.literal: In Yongxi Chu memorialized asking that he be allowed to take the jinshi examination; Taizong, because he was a great house's son, specially summoned him to trial in the inner office, appointed Secretariat Director, granted gold and purple, and promoted him repeatedly to Director of the Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi Chu asked that Pi sit for jinshi; Taizong specially tested him in the inner office, made him Secretariat Director with gold and purple, and promoted him to Transport Director.

sentences.zh: 嘗知新淦縣，又知衡州。

translations.literal: He once governed Xin'gan County and also Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He once governed Xin'gan and Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟治卒，以將作少監起復，俄為三司戶部判官，卒於光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhi died Pi was appointed Acting Master of Works on mourning leave, soon became Vice Director of the Three Departments Household Office, and died as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei Zhi's death Pi was made Acting Master of Works on mourning leave, then Three Departments vice director, and died as Imperial Household vice director.

sentences.zh: 子 惟濟

translations.literal: Son: Wei Ji
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wei Ji

sentences.zh: 惟濟字岩夫。

translations.literal: Wei Ji, courtesy name Yanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji, courtesy name Yanfu.

sentences.zh: 生七歲，俶封漢南國王，奏補本府元從指揮使，曆諸衛將軍，領恩州刺史，改東染院使，真拜封州刺史。

translations.literal: At seven, when Chu was created King of Hannan, he memorialized appointing him commander of the original followers of his domain; he passed through various guards generals, held Enzhou, became Eastern Dyeing commissioner, and was formally appointed prefect of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, when Chu became King of Hannan, he was made domain follower commander, rose through guards posts, held Enzhou, became Eastern Dyeing commissioner, and was appointed prefect of Feng.

sentences.zh: 真宗祀汾陰還，燕近臣苑中，命惟濟射，一發中的。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong returned from sacrificing at Fenyin he feasted close ministers in the garden and ordered Wei Ji to shoot; one arrow hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the Fenyin rites Zhenzong feasted ministers in the garden and had Wei Ji shoot; his first arrow struck home.

sentences.zh: 故事，刺史射不解箭，帝賜解之，且賜襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: By precedent prefects shooting did not unstring the arrow; the emperor granted him unstringing and also granted court robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: By custom prefects did not unstring after shooting; the emperor allowed it and gave court robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 其後請試郡，命知絳州。

translations.literal: Afterward he asked to trial governing a prefecture and was appointed to govern Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to try governing a commandery and was made prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 民有條桑者，盜奪桑不能得，乃自創其臂，誣桑主欲殺人，久係不能辨。

translations.literal: A man who planted mulberry trees had a thief seize his mulberry and fail to get it; the man then cut his own arm and falsely accused the mulberry owner of attempted murder, and was long detained without the case being cleared.
translations.idiomatic: A mulberry grower was robbed; failing to catch the thief he cut his own arm and accused the owner of attempted murder, and the case dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 惟濟取盜與之食，視之，盜以左手舉匕箸，惟濟曰：「以右手創人者上重下輕，今汝創特下重，正用左手傷右臂，非爾自為之邪？」

translations.literal: Wei Ji had food brought to the thief; watching him, the thief lifted spoon and chopsticks with his left hand. Wei Ji said, "One who wounds with the right hand strikes heavy above and light below; your wound is especially heavy below—you used your left hand to injure your right arm. Did you not do this yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: He fed the thief and saw him eat with his left hand. Wei Ji said, "A right-handed blow is heavy above, light below—your wound is heavy below only; you used your left on your right arm. You did this yourself, did you not?"

sentences.zh: 辭遂服。

translations.literal: The confession was then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The thief confessed.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，謂宰相向敏中曰：「惟濟試守郡輒明辨，後必為能吏矣！」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he told Chief Minister Xiang Minzhong, "Wei Ji on trial governing a commandery at once judged clearly—later he will surely be a capable official!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Xiang Minzhong, "On his first trial as prefect Wei Ji judged clearly—he will be a capable official."

sentences.zh: 徙潞州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 民相驚有外寇，奔城而仆者相枕藉，惟濟從容行視，從騎甚省，民乃安。

translations.literal: The people were alarmed that foreign raiders had come and rushed to the city, falling atop one another; Wei Ji walked the scene at ease with very few mounted followers, and the people were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of invasion sent people rushing to the walls in heaps; Wei Ji toured calmly with a small escort and the people settled.

sentences.zh: 遷永州團練使，改知成德軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regimental commander of Yongzhou and changed to govern the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yongzhou regimental commander, then governed Chengde.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Renzong succeeded he was promoted to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At Renzong's accession he was made acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 民有偽作白金質取緡錢者，其家來告，惟濟曰：「第聲言被盜，示以重購，質者當來責餘直，即得之矣。」

translations.literal: A man counterfeited white gold quality to obtain cash; his family reported it. Wei Ji said, "Only proclaim that you were robbed, offer a heavy reward, and when the counterfeiter comes to demand the balance you will get him."
translations.idiomatic: When a man counterfeited platinum for cash, Wei Ji said, "Announce a robbery and offer a large reward—when he returns for the balance you will catch him."

sentences.zh: 已而果然，乃杖配之。

translations.literal: Before long it was indeed so, and he was beaten and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it happened as he said; the man was flogged and exiled.

sentences.zh: 以吉州防禦使留再任，遷虔州觀察使，知定州。

translations.literal: As defense commissioner of Jizhou he was retained for another term, promoted to observation commissioner of Qianzhou, and appointed to govern Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Retained as Jizhou defense commissioner, he became Qianzhou observation commissioner and governed Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 有婦人待前妻子不仁，至燒銅錢灼臂，惟濟取婦人所生兒置雪中，械婦人往視兒死。

translations.literal: A woman was unkind to her husband's children by a former wife, even burning copper cash to scald an arm; Wei Ji placed the woman's own child in snow and shackled the woman to watch the child die.
translations.idiomatic: A stepmother burned copper cash on a child's arm; Wei Ji set her own infant in snow and chained her to watch it die.

sentences.zh: 其慘毒多此類。

translations.literal: His cruelty was mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His punishments were often of this kind.

sentences.zh: 遷武昌軍節度觀察留後，改保靜軍留後。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military observation commissioner and acting commissioner of the Wuchang army, then changed to acting commissioner of the Baojing army.
translations.idiomatic: He became Wuchang observation and acting commissioner, then Baojing acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 惟濟喜賓客，豐宴犒，家無餘貲，帝賜白金二千兩，所負公使錢七百餘萬。

translations.literal: Wei Ji delighted in guests and gave lavish feasts and rewards; his house had no surplus, and the emperor granted two thousand taels of white gold for public envoy debts exceeding seven million.
translations.idiomatic: He loved guests and feasted lavishly until penniless; the emperor gave two thousand taels of white gold against over seven million in public debts.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平江節度使，諡宣惠。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted military commissioner of Pingjiang with posthumous name Extending Grace.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Pingjiang military commissioner, posthumous name Extending Grace.

sentences.zh: 遣使護葬事，賜賻錢二百萬、絹千匹。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to oversee the funeral and grant two million in funeral money and a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys directed the funeral with two million cash and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 有《玉季集》二十卷。

translations.literal: He had the Jade Season Collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jade Season Collection in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 惟濟有吏幹，能戢下而性苛忍，所至牽蔓滿獄。

translations.literal: Wei Ji had administrative talent and could restrain subordinates but was harsh and cruel; wherever he went the prisons were full from extended cases.
translations.idiomatic: He governed ably and controlled subordinates but was harsh; his prisons were always crowded.

sentences.zh: 重囚棄市，或斷手足，探肝膽，用以威眾。

translations.literal: For serious criminals at the execution ground he sometimes severed hands and feet or extracted liver and gall to awe the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: At executions he sometimes severed limbs or removed organs to terrify onlookers.

sentences.zh: 觀者色動，而惟濟自若也。

translations.literal: Spectators changed color while Wei Ji remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers blanched while he remained calm.

sentences.zh: 弟 儼

translations.literal: Younger brother: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Yan

sentences.zh: 儼字誠允，俶之異母弟也。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Chengyun, was Chu's younger brother by a different mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, courtesy name Chengyun, was Chu's half-brother.

sentences.zh: 本名信，淳化初改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Xin; at the beginning of Chunhua it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Xin, he was renamed at the start of Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 幼為沙門，及長，頗謹慎好學。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; when grown he was quite cautious and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was a monk; grown, he was careful and studious.

sentences.zh: 俶襲國封，命為鎮東軍安撫副使。

translations.literal: When Chu succeeded to the state enfeoffment he was appointed Pacification Vice Commissioner of the Zhendong army.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu took the throne Yan was made Zhendong Pacification Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周顯德四年，奏署衢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande of Zhou he memorialized appointing him prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Xiande 4 he was appointed prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖平揚州，俶遣儼入賀，命閣門副使武懷節齎詔迎勞，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Yangzhou Chu sent Yan to congratulate; Vice Commissioner of the Gate Wu Huaijie was sent with an edict to welcome and honor him, with very rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Yangzhou Chu sent Yan to congratulate; Wu Huaijie welcomed him with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 及歸，又賜玉帶、名馬、錦彩、器皿。

translations.literal: On his return he was again granted jade belt, famous horses, brocade, and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he received jade belt, fine horses, brocade, and vessels.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，代兄偡知湖州，充宣德軍安撫使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he replaced his elder brother Wei as prefect of Huzhou and served as Pacification Commissioner of the Xuande army.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 3 he replaced his brother as Huzhou prefect and Xuande Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俶奉詔攻毗陵，命儼督漕運。

translations.literal: When Chu received orders to attack Piling he ordered Yan to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Piling campaign Chu had Yan oversee grain transport.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，從俶之請，授新、媯、儒等州觀察使，仍知湖州，儼兄儀為慎、瑞、師等州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, at Chu's request, he was appointed observation commissioner of Xin, Gui, Ru, and other prefectures while still governing Huzhou; Yan's elder brother Yi was observation commissioner of Shen, Rui, Shi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 Chu had him made observation commissioner over Xin, Gui, Ru and others while governing Huzhou; brother Yi held Shen, Rui, Shi and others.

sentences.zh: 入朝，以儼為隨州觀察使，儀為金州觀察使。

translations.literal: Coming to court, Yan was made observation commissioner of Suizhou and Yi of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At court Yan became Suizhou observation commissioner and Yi Jinzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 侍祠郊宮，特召升儼班於節度使之次。

translations.literal: Attending the suburban sacrifice in the palace precinct, he was specially summoned to advance Yan's court rank to just below military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban rites Yan's court rank was raised to just below military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 儀卒，儼換金州。

translations.literal: When Yi died Yan was transferred to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died Yan moved to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 常從幸天駟監，會賜從官馬，太宗敕有司曰：「錢儼儒者，宜擇馴馬給之。」

translations.literal: He often followed on visits to the Imperial Stud; when horses were granted to followers Taizong ordered the authorities, "Qian Yan is a Confucian—choose gentle horses for him."
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Stud, when horses were given to followers Taizong said, "Yan is a scholar—give him tame horses."

sentences.zh: 未幾，出判和州，在職十七年。

translations.literal: Before long he went out to judge Hezhou and served seventeen years in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned Hezhou and served seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，卒，年六十七，贈昭化軍節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping he died at the age of sixty-seven and was posthumously granted military commissioner of the Zhaohua army.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 6 he died at sixty-seven and was posthumously made Zhaohua military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 儼嗜學，博涉經史。

translations.literal: Yan loved learning and broadly studied the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved learning and read widely in classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 少夢人遺以大硯，自是樂為文辭，頗敏速富贍，當時國中詞翰多出其手。

translations.literal: In youth he dreamed someone gave him a large inkstone; from then he delighted in literary composition, was quite quick and prolific, and at the time most of the state's documents came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of receiving a great inkstone and thereafter wrote swiftly; most state documents were his.

sentences.zh: 歸京師，與朝廷文士遊，歌詠不絕。

translations.literal: In the capital he associated with court literati and never ceased singing and composing.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he mingled with literati and wrote constantly.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，嘗獻《皇猷錄》，咸平又獻《光聖錄》，並有詔嘉答。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he once presented the Records of the Imperial Design; in Xianping he again presented the Records of the Sagely Radiance—both received edicts of praise.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua he presented Records of the Imperial Design; in Xianping Records of the Sagely Radiance—both praised by edict.

sentences.zh: 所著有前集五十卷、後集二十四卷、《吳越備史》十五卷、《備史遺事》五卷、《忠懿王勳業志》三卷，又作《貴溪叟自敘傳》一卷。

translations.literal: His works included an earlier collection of fifty juan, a later collection of twenty-four juan, Fifteen juan of the Supplementary History of Wu and Yue, five juan of Remnant Events of the Supplementary History, three juan of the Record of the Meritorious Achievements of the Loyal and Gracious King, and one juan of the Old Man of Guixi's Autobiography.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote earlier and later collections, Supplementary History of Wu-Yue and related works, and an autobiography—seventy-plus juan in all.

sentences.zh: 善飲酒，百卮不醉，居外郡嘗患無敵，或言一軍校差可倫擬，儼問其狀，曰：「飲益多，手益恭。」

translations.literal: He loved drinking and did not become drunk after a hundred cups; governing outer commanderies he once grieved having no equal, and when told a certain army officer might compare, he asked his manner and was told, "The more he drinks the more respectful his hands become."
translations.idiomatic: He could drink a hundred cups without drunkenness; told an officer might match him, he asked how and heard, "The more he drinks the more carefully he holds his cup."

sentences.zh: 儼曰：「此亦變常，非善飲也。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "That is also a change from the norm—not true drinking."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "That is mere change of habit—not true drinking."

sentences.zh: 姪 昱

translations.literal: Nephew: Yu
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Yu

sentences.zh: 昱字就之，忠獻王佐之長子。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Jiuzhi, was the eldest son of the Loyal and Offering King Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, courtesy name Jiuzhi, was eldest son of King Zuo.

sentences.zh: 佐薨，昱尚幼，國人立倧，遂以昱為咸寧、大安二宮使。

translations.literal: When Zuo died Yu was still young; the people enthroned Cong and made Yu commissioner of the Xianning and Da'an palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo died Yu was a child; Cong was enthroned and Yu made commissioner of two palaces.

sentences.zh: 俶嗣國，承製授秀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chu succeeded he issued a commission appointing Yu prefect of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu succeeded he made Yu prefect of Xiu.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，俶遣昱入貢，與江南使同侍宴射於後苑。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate Chu sent Yu to present tribute; with the Jiangnan envoy he attended a banquet and archery in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu's accession Chu sent Yu with tribute; he feasted and shot in the rear garden with the Jiangnan envoy.

sentences.zh: 江南使先中的，令昱解之，昱應弦而中，賜以玉帶。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan envoy hit the mark first; Yu was ordered to unstring and hit at the sound of the bowstring, and was granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan envoy hit first; Yu was told to unstring and struck at the sound; he received a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 及平蜀，復來賀。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he came again to congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell he came again to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 歸國，為台州刺史。

translations.literal: Returning to his state he became prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he became Taizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 俶得福州，命昱守之。

translations.literal: When Chu took Fuzhou he ordered Yu to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu took Fuzhou he left Yu to guard it.

sentences.zh: 王師討江南，為東面水陸行營應援使。

translations.literal: When the imperial army chastised Jiangnan he was Eastern Front land-and-water Support Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan war he was Eastern Front land-and-water support commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從俶入朝，授白州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Chu to court he was appointed prefect of Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Following Chu to court he was made prefect of Bai.

sentences.zh: 昱好學，多聚書，喜吟詠，多與中朝卿大夫唱酬。

translations.literal: Yu loved learning, gathered many books, delighted in chanting and composing, and often exchanged poems with central court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and poetry and often exchanged verse with court ministers.

sentences.zh: 嘗與沙門讚寧談竹事，迭錄所記，昱得百餘條，因集為《竹譜》三卷。

translations.literal: Once with the monk Zanning he discussed bamboo, each recording notes; Yu got more than a hundred entries and compiled them into three juan of the Bamboo Canon.
translations.idiomatic: With monk Zanning he debated bamboo lore, gathered over a hundred entries, and compiled three juan of the Bamboo Canon.

sentences.zh: 俄獻《太平興國錄》。

translations.literal: Soon he presented the Records of Taiping Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He soon presented Records of Taiping Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 求換台省官，令學士院召試制誥三篇，改秘書監，判尚書都省。

translations.literal: He asked to exchange for a central ministry post; the Hanlin Academy was ordered to test him on three edict drafts, and he was changed to Director of the Secretariat supervising the Secretariat and Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a central post; tested on three edicts, he became Secretariat Director supervising the ministries.

sentences.zh: 時新葺省署，昱撰記奏禦，又嘗以鍾、王墨跡八卷為獻，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: When the ministries were newly rebuilt Yu composed a memorial account and presented it; he also once presented eight scrolls of Zhong and Wang ink traces and received an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When offices were rebuilt he wrote the memorial and presented eight scrolls of Zhong and Wang calligraphy, winning praise.

sentences.zh: 出知宋州，改工部侍郎，曆典壽、泗、宿三州，率無善政。

translations.literal: Going out to govern Songzhou he was changed to Vice Minister of Works and passed through Shou, Si, and Su prefectures, in each case without good government.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Songzhou, became Vice Minister of Works, then Shou, Si, and Su—none with good rule.

sentences.zh: 至道中，郊祀，當進秩，太宗曰：「昱貴家子無檢操，不宜任丞郎。」

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era at the suburban sacrifice he was due for promotion; Taizong said, "Yu is a nobleman's son without restraint—he should not hold director and vice-director posts."
translations.idiomatic: At Zhidao suburban rites he was due promotion; Taizong said, "Yu is unrestrained nobility—unsuited to ministry posts."

sentences.zh: 以為郢州團練使。

translations.literal: He was made regimental commander of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Ezhou regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，表入朝，以病不及陛見，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he memorialized to come to court but, ill, could not ascend the hall and died at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 he came to court but was too ill for audience and died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 昱善筆劄，工尺牘，太祖嘗取觀賞之，賜以御書金花扇及《急就章》。

translations.literal: Yu was skilled at letters and craft in formal documents; Taizu once took them to admire and granted an imperial gold-flower fan and the Rapid Writing Primer.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at letters and documents, he won Taizu's praise and received an imperial fan and the Rapid Writing Primer.

sentences.zh: 昱聰敏能覆棋，工琴畫，飲酒至鬥餘不亂。

translations.literal: Yu was clever and could replay chess from memory, was accomplished at zither and painting, and could drink more than a dou without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Clever at blindfold chess, zither, and painting, he could drink a dou without losing composure.

sentences.zh: 善諧謔，生平交舊終日談宴，未曾犯一人家諱。

translations.literal: He was good at banter and all his life associated with old friends in daily talk and feasts without once violating a household taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Witty in company, he feasted with friends daily and never once spoke another's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left twenty juan of writings.

sentences.zh: 然貪猥縱肆，無名節可稱。

translations.literal: Yet he was greedy, base, and unrestrained, with no reputation to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy and dissolute, with no reputation worth naming.

sentences.zh: 生子百數。

translations.literal: He fathered sons by the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons numbering in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 涉，雍熙中進士及第。

translations.literal: She passed the jinshi in the Yongxi era.
translations.idiomatic: Son She passed jinshi in Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 絳，至內殿承製、閣門祗候，累典郡，頗以幹力稱。

translations.literal: Jiang rose to Inner Hall Edict Drafter and Gate Attendant, repeatedly governed commanderies, and was praised for administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang became Inner Hall edict drafter and Gate Attendant, governed several commanderies, and was noted for ability.

sentences.zh: 俶之群從又有台州刺史仰之子昭序，字著明，好學喜聚書，書多親寫。

translations.literal: Among Chu's clan kindred there was also Zhaoxu, courtesy name Zhuming, son of Yang, prefect of Taizhou—he loved learning and gathering books and copied many himself.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Zhaoxu, courtesy name Zhuming, son of Taizhou prefect Yang, loved books and copied many himself.

sentences.zh: 知通利軍，以勤幹聞，至如京副使。

translations.literal: Governing Tongli Army he was known for diligence and ability and rose to Vice Commissioner of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Governing Tongli he was known for diligence and reached Capital Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 衢州刺史偓之子昭度，字九齡，至供奉官。

translations.literal: Zhaodu, courtesy name Jiuling, son of Wo, prefect of Quzhou, rose to Attendant of Offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu, courtesy name Jiuling, son of Quzhou prefect Wo, reached Attendant of Offerings.

sentences.zh: 俊敏工為詩，多警句，有集十卷，蘇易簡為序行於世。

translations.literal: Quick and clever at poetry with many striking lines, he had a collection of ten juan prefaced by Su Yijian and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Quick at verse with many striking lines, he left ten juan prefaced by Su Yijian.

sentences.zh: 孫 承祐

translations.literal: Relative: Sun Chengyou
translations.idiomatic: Relative: Sun Chengyou

sentences.zh: 孫承祐，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Sun Chengyou was a native of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chengyou came from Qiantang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俶納其姊為妃，因擢處要職，累遷浙江東道鹽鐵副使、鎮海鎮東兩軍節度副使、知靜海軍節度事。

translations.literal: Chu took his elder sister as consort and therefore promoted him to important posts, rising repeatedly to Vice Commissioner of Zhe East Route Salt and Iron, vice military commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, and commissioner of Jinghai army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chu married his sister and promoted him to salt commissioner, Zhenhai-Zhendong vice commissioner, and Jinghai commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，隨俶子惟濬入貢，詔授光祿大夫、檢校太保、鎮東鎮海等軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao he followed Chu's son Wei Jun to present tribute and was appointed by edict Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Guardian, and acting military affairs commissioner of Zhendong, Zhenhai, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaibao he followed Wei Jun with tribute and was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Guardian, and Zhendong-Zhenhai acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俶又私署中吳軍節度。

translations.literal: Chu also privately appointed him military commissioner of the Central Wu army.
translations.idiomatic: Chu also privately made him Central Wu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，俶復遣承祐入貢，賜襲衣、玉帶、鞍勒馬、黃金器五百兩、銀器三千兩、雜彩五千匹，且令諭旨於俶，將有事於江表。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Chu again sent Chengyou with tribute and granted court robes, jade belt, saddle and bridle with horse, five hundred taels of gold vessels, three thousand taels of silver vessels, and five thousand bolts of mixed silks, and ordered him to convey the imperial intent to Chu that action was planned in the Jiangbiao region.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Chu sent him with tribute and rich gifts, telling him to say the court would act in the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 及王師渡江，命內客省使丁德裕率步騎一千，詔俶以所部與德裕會攻常、潤。

translations.literal: When the imperial army crossed the Yangzi the Inner Palace Envoy Ding Deyu led one thousand infantry and cavalry; an edict ordered Chu to unite his forces with Deyu to attack Chang and Run.
translations.idiomatic: When the army crossed the Yangzi Ding Deyu led a thousand guards; Chu was to join him against Chang and Run.

sentences.zh: 承祐從俶克毗陵，功居多，詔改中吳軍為平江軍，真授承祐節。

translations.literal: Chengyou followed Chu in taking Piling with the greatest merit; an edict changed Central Wu army to Pingjiang army and formally appointed Chengyou commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chu to Piling with chief merit; Central Wu became Pingjiang and he received formal commission.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，俶來朝，盡獻其地，徙承祐泰寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Taiping Xingguo when Chu came to court and surrendered all his territory Chengyou was moved to military commissioner of the Taining army.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu surrendered his lands Chengyou was made Taining military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，從幸大名，留知府事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed the visit to Daming and was left to govern prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he followed the Daming visit and was left to govern there.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，改知滑州，數月卒，贈太子太師，中使護葬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was changed to govern Huazhou and died several months later, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with a palace envoy overseeing burial.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he governed Huazhou, died months later, and was posthumously made Heir Apparent Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 承祐在浙右日，憑藉親寵，恣為奢侈，每一飲宴，凡殺物命千數，常膳亦數十品方下箸。

translations.literal: While in the Zhe region Chengyou relied on kin favor and indulged in luxury; each feast killed animals by the thousand, and even daily meals required dozens of dishes before chopsticks were taken up.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhe he lived luxuriously on kin favor; each feast killed a thousand animals and daily meals required dozens of dishes.

sentences.zh: 所居室中，爇龍腦日不下數兩。

translations.literal: In his dwelling dragon's brain incense burned no less than several taels a day.
translations.idiomatic: His rooms burned several taels of dragon's brain daily.

sentences.zh: 從車駕北征，以橐駝負大斛貯水養魚自隨。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign with the imperial carriage he carried fish in a great tub of water on a camel.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he carried a camel-load tub of water with live fish.

sentences.zh: 至幽州南村落間，日已旰，西京留守石守信與其子駙馬都尉保吉及近臣十數人尚未朝食，適遇承祐，即延所止幕舍中，膾魚具食，窮極水陸，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Reaching a village south of Youzhou at dusk, Western Capital Regent Shi Shouxin with his son the Imperial Son-in-Law Shi Baoji and a dozen close ministers had not yet eaten; meeting Chengyou they extended him to their tent, served sliced fish and a full feast of land and water delicacies, and all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At a Youzhou village at dusk Shi Shouxin and courtiers, unfed, met Chengyou and received a feast of land and sea delicacies that astonished all.

sentences.zh: 承祐少時，嘗夢人以蓍草一本，增其一而授之。

translations.literal: In youth Chengyou once dreamed a man gave him one stalk of yarrow divination grass, adding one more and handing it to him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he dreamed a man gave him one stalk of divination grass, then added another.

sentences.zh: 既寤，以語所親曰：「『大衍之數五十，其用四十有九』，今增其一，我壽止於此乎。」

translations.literal: On waking he told those close to him, "'The Great Expansion number is fifty, of which forty-nine are used'—now one is added; my life ends here, does it not?"
translations.idiomatic: Awake he said, "The Great Expansion uses forty-nine of fifty—one was added; my life ends here."

sentences.zh: 果五十而卒。

translations.literal: Indeed at fifty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty as foretold.

sentences.zh: 子誘，至駕部郎中，出為淮南節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Son You rose to Director of the Transport Office and went out as acting military affairs commissioner of the Huainan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Son You became Transport Director and Huainan acting military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 附 沈承禮

translations.literal: Appendix: Shen Chengli
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Shen Chengli

sentences.zh: 沈承禮，湖州烏程人。

translations.literal: Shen Chengli was a native of Wucheng in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chengli came from Wucheng in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐辟置幕府，署處州刺史。

translations.literal: Qian Liu recruited him to his staff headquarters and appointed him prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu brought him into his staff and made him prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鏐子元瓘以女妻之，署為府中右職，出為台州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu's son Yuan Guan gave him a daughter in marriage, appointed him to a senior post in the headquarters, and sent him out as prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guan married him to his daughter, gave him a senior headquarters post, and later sent him out as Taizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 元瓘卒，子佐嗣，以承禮掌親兵。

translations.literal: When Yuan Guan died his son Zuo succeeded, and Chengli was placed in command of the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Guan died and Zuo succeeded, Chengli commanded the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 俶襲位，命知威武軍節度事，充兩浙都鈐轄使。

translations.literal: When Chu succeeded to the throne he was ordered to manage Weiwu army circuit affairs and serve as overall commander of military affairs in the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu took power he was made to manage the Weiwu circuit and overall commander of Zhe military affairs.

sentences.zh: 王師征江南，俶遣承禮率水陸數萬人助平毗陵，因攻潤州。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Jiangnan Chu sent Chengli at the head of tens of thousands by land and water to help pacify Piling, then advanced to attack Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan campaign Chu sent Chengli with tens of thousands by land and sea to help take Piling, then besieged Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 城中兵夜出焚外柵，諸將皆欲馳救，承禮曰：「古人有言，擊東南而備西北者，此之謂也。」

translations.literal: Troops in the city came out at night and burned the outer palisade; all the generals wished to gallop to the rescue, but Chengli said, "The ancients said that to strike the southeast while preparing the northwest—this is what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: At night the garrison burned the outer palisade; other generals wanted to rush to help, but Chengli said, "The ancients spoke of feinting southeast while guarding northwest—this is that stratagem."

sentences.zh: 命士皆擐甲蓐食，堅壁不動。

translations.literal: He ordered the men to don armor and eat in bed, holding the walls firm without moving.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men arm and eat in camp, holding the walls and refusing to stir.

sentences.zh: 他壘不設備者悉驚擾，獨承禮所部敵人不敢窺。

translations.literal: Other camps that made no preparations were all alarmed and thrown into disorder; only Chengli's command—the enemy did not dare spy on it.
translations.idiomatic: Other camps without preparation fell into panic; only Chengli's sector did the enemy not dare probe.

sentences.zh: 丹陽平，遂率兵抵建業。

translations.literal: When Danyang was pacified he then led his troops to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: After Danyang fell he marched on to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 李煜歸朝，錄其功，真授福州節制。

translations.literal: When Li Yu came to court his merit was recorded and he was formally appointed military commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu submitted, Chengli's merit was recorded and he was formally made Fuzhou military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，俶盡獻浙右地，徙承禮鎮密州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, when Chu surrendered all the Zhe right territories, Chengli was transferred to govern Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taiping Xingguo, when Chu surrendered all Zhe lands, Chengli was moved to govern Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 廢朝二日，贈太子太師，中使護葬。

translations.literal: Court was suspended two days; he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and a palace envoy oversaw the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned two days; he was posthumously made Heir Apparent Grand Preceptor, with a palace envoy directing burial.

sentences.zh: 初，秦王廷美之敗也，有司按驗，俶、惟濬、孫承祐及陳洪進皆嘗有贈遺，獨承禮無焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince of Qin Tingmei fell, the authorities investigated; Chu, Wei Jun, Sun Chengyou, and Chen Hongjin had all at times given gifts, but Chengli alone had not.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Tingmei of Qin fell, investigators found Chu, Wei Jun, Sun Chengyou, and Chen Hongjin had all given him gifts—Chengli alone had not.
